scheme: UMC self-disclosed that it submitted claims for mid-level practitioner services at physician rates in its urgent care and primary care clinics and paid remuneration to a physician and practice through additional payments for professional services, to a physician in the form of free space to see private dental patients, and to a practice and two physician managers in the form of free space purportedly leased from UMC.

title: Summit Healthcare Association Agreed to Pay $2.8 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying and Receiving Improper Remuneration in the Form of Excessive Rental Fees, Excessive Compensation, and Free Staffing Services
scheme: OIG alleged that Summit paid a physician excessive rental fees under a lease agreement, made excessive compensation payments to an oncologist outside the scope of the oncologist's employment, and received free staffing services from two local hospices.

title: Wound Graft Company Owners Sentenced for $1.2B Health Care Fraud and Agree to Pay $309M to Resolve Civil Liability Under the False Claims Act
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Arizona
scheme: The owners of Arizona wound graft companies caused over $1.2 billion in false and fraudulent claims to be submitted to Medicare and other health insurance programs for medically unnecessary wound grafts ordered as a result of illegal kickbacks and applied to elderly and terminally ill patients.

title: Parkville Mother and Daughter Sentenced in $3.6 Million Medicaid Fraud Scheme
scheme: Saunders operated two behavioral health companies that submitted fraudulent Medicaid claims for Psychiatric Rehabilitation Program services that were not provided, using forged signatures, fake patient records, and stolen identities of providers and Medicaid recipients, causing Maryland Medicaid to reimburse $3,672,958.66.

title: Brian August, MD Agreed to Be Excluded for 15 Years for Issuing Prescriptions that Did Not Have a Legitimate Medical Purpose
scheme: August issued controlled substance prescriptions that were not prescribed for a legitimate medical purpose and were not eligible for reimbursement by Medicare or Texas Medicaid.

title: Pharmacist Sentenced to Over Six Years in Prison for $6 Million Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: A pharmacist and a co-conspirator billed health care benefit programs for prescription medications that were not ordered by a doctor and never dispensed to patients, using forged prescriptions, at three Michigan pharmacies.

title: Community Hospital San Bernadino Agreed to Pay $112,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Community Hospital San Bernadino employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Canton Man Sentenced for Multi-Million-Dollar Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Gidwani conspired to own and operate a durable medical equipment company that paid telemarketing companies for orthotic brace orders and submitted over $4 million in Medicare claims for equipment that was medically unnecessary, not wanted by beneficiaries and tainted by kickbacks.

title: St. John's Regional Medical Center Agreed to Pay $357,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: St. John's Regional Medical Center self-disclosed that it employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Former Community Support Worker Pleads Guilty to Defrauding District of Columbia Medicaid Program
scheme: Jalloh submitted encounter notes for community support services she did not provide and overbilled for services she allegedly provided to District Medicaid beneficiaries, causing the District's Medicaid program to pay over $234,500.

title: Former St. Louis Area Pediatrician Admits Exchanging Prescriptions for Sex Acts
district: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Missouri, Eastern
scheme: A pediatrician admitted issuing prescriptions for controlled substances with no legitimate medical purpose in exchange for sex acts, nude photos or cash, including prescribing in others' names to use their insurance benefits, causing $114,480 in losses to Medicare, Missouri Medicaid and Illinois Medicaid.

title: Owner Of Physical Rehabilitation Company Pleads Guilty To Submitting More Than $20 Million In Fraudulent Medical Bills To Health Benefit Programs
scheme: The owner of a physical rehabilitation company engaged in a scheme to defraud health benefit programs through the submission of more than $20 million in fraudulent claims.

title: Central Emergency Medical Services Agreed to Pay $20,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: CEMS self-disclosed that it employed an individual it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Spokane Physician Pays $120,000 to Resolve Allegations He Prescribed Controlled Substances Without Legitimate Medical Purpose
scheme: Between 2017 and 2025 a licensed physician issued over 1,400 prescriptions for controlled substances to thirteen identified patients that lacked legitimate medical purposes or were outside the usual course of professional practice, failing to address red flags of substance abuse.

title: Recovery Centers of America Agrees to Pay $2 Million to Resolve Allegations That It Violated the Controlled Substances Act and the False Claims Act by Mishandling Controlled Substances and Providing Inadequate Treatment Services
scheme: Recovery Centers of America agreed to pay $1,000,000 to resolve allegations that it failed to comply with Controlled Substances Act provisions designed to prevent diversion of controlled substances and an additional $1,000,000 to resolve allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by billing the government for drug and alcohol treatment services it failed to adequately provide.

title: AG’s Office Secures Guilty Plea From Haverhill Defendant For Defrauding PCA Program
scheme: Defendant pleaded guilty to defrauding MassHealth's personal care attendant program.

title: Telehealth Company Agrees to Pay $300,000 to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - New Hampshire
scheme: LifeWorks Counseling Associates and its owner submitted claims and received reimbursement from Medicaid for services provided by Erik Alonso, who was excluded from federal health care programs at the time.

title: Attorney General’s Medicaid Fraud and Vulnerable Victims Unit Secures a $400,000 Settlement and Corporate Oversight of Orchard Hill Rehabilitation and Health Care Center
scheme: Orchard Hill allegedly violated the Maryland False Health Claims Act by providing substandard care to residents whose care was paid for by Medicaid, including wound care inadequacies, inadequate nutrition and hydration, regulatory violations, preventable falls, and inadequate staffing.

title: H. Brady Millican, III Agreed to Be Excluded for 3 Years for Allegedly Paying Improper Remuneration
scheme: Millican, on behalf of Admera Health, LLC, paid marketers commission payments that were determined in a manner that took into account the volume and value of genetic testing referrals for which payment was made by Federal health care programs.

title: Coastline Emergency Medical Services and SouthCoast Emergency Medical Services Agreed to Pay $162,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting False Claims for Emergency Ambulance Services
scheme: Coastline and SouthCoast submitted claims for emergency ambulance transportation to destinations, such as skilled nursing facilities and patient residences, that should have been billed at the lower non-emergency rate.

title: Option Care Health Agreed to Pay $719,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Improper Remuneration in the Form of Referral Based Compensation
scheme: OIG alleged that Option Care paid remuneration to a health care system and a physician practice in the form of compensation for physician services that varied with the volume of parenteral infusion therapy services referred to Option Care, where the physician services were reimbursable separately.

title: Illinois Men Face Additional Charges for Health Care Fraud and Money Laundering Conspiracy
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Two brothers who owned and controlled four clinical laboratories in Illinois and California allegedly submitted over $293 million in fraudulent claims for COVID-19 laboratory testing services that were never provided and laundered the proceeds through businesses and purchases of real estate, gold bars, watches and vehicles.

title: Midwest Surgery Center Agreed to Pay $274,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: After self-disclosing to OIG, Midwest Surgery Center submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed nurse.

title: Brentwood Springs Agreed to Pay $54,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Brentwood submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed therapist.

title: Williamsport and Deercreek Emergency Squad Agreed to Pay $160,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that WADES employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Virginia Laboratory to Pay $758,000 to Settle Allegations of Kickbacks to Doctors and Marketers
scheme: NEXT agreed to pay at least $758,000 to resolve False Claims Act allegations involving illegal kickbacks to doctors and marketers.

title: CEO of Fresno-based Health Care Company Arrested at San Francisco Airport for an Alleged $7 Million Scheme to Defraud the Department of Veterans Affairs
scheme: The CEO of a home health care company submitted approximately 10,000 false claims to the Department of Veterans Affairs for in-home care hours not actually rendered, including care billed for veterans who were already dead, resulting in $7 million in reimbursements.

title: Indian National Sentenced To Prison For Medicare Fraud Scheme That Stole More Than $1 Million In Taxpayer Funds
scheme: Asif conspired with others to bill Medicare for COVID-19 tests and other respiratory illness tests that had not been ordered or performed through American Labworks LLC.

title: Largest North Carolina Behavioral Health Practice Agrees to Pay $1.9 Million to Resolve Allegedly False Medicare Claims
scheme: Mindpath and former officers allegedly billed Medicare for psychotherapy and medication management sessions without documentation of separate and distinct psychotherapy treatments from 2018 to 2020.

title: Georgia Man Sentenced for $24M Kickback and Medicare Fraud Conspiracy
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Georgia, Southern
scheme: Moore instructed a network of recruiters to induce Medicare beneficiaries to accept medically unnecessary genetic tests, received approximately $4.3 million in kickbacks for referrals of beneficiary information, DNA specimens and doctors' orders, paid kickbacks to recruiters, and concealed the payments with sham invoices while associated laboratories billed Medicare approximately $24 million.

title: Attorney General Alan Wilson announces two Upstate Medicaid providers charged with fraud
scheme: Stewart, owner of Above and Beyond Care Services, LLC, and Weiss, an employee, conspired to submit false employee timesheets to SCDHHS claiming personal care and respite services had been provided to a Medicaid beneficiary when the services were not provided.

title: Palos Community Hospital Agreed to Pay $129,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by Unlicensed Individuals
scheme: OIG alleged that Palos Community Hospital submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed nurse and an unlicensed speech language pathologist.

title: Indian national sentenced to prison for Medicare fraud scheme that stole more than $1 million in taxpayer funds
scheme: Asif conspired with others to bill Medicare for COVID-19 tests and other respiratory illness tests that had not been ordered or performed through American Labworks LLC.

title: Largest North Carolina Behavioral Health Practice Agrees to Pay $1.9 Million to Resolve Allegedly False Medicare Claims
scheme: Mindpath Care Centers and three former officers paid $1,900,000 to resolve allegedly false Medicare claims billed for psychotherapy and related services.

title: Georgia Man Sentenced for $24M Kickback and Medicare Fraud Conspiracy
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Georgia, Southern
scheme: Moore instructed a network of recruiters to induce Medicare beneficiaries to accept medically unnecessary genetic tests, received approximately $4.3 million in kickbacks for referring beneficiary information, DNA specimens and doctors' orders, and concealed the payments with sham invoices.

title: U.S. Attorney Announces $37.76 Million Settlement With CVS For Over-Dispensing Insulin Pens To Patients
scheme: From 2010 through 2020, CVS improperly requested and received government healthcare program reimbursement for premature refills, dispensed more insulin pens than patients needed according to their prescriptions, and under-reported the days-of-supply of insulin that its pharmacies dispensed.

title: Owner of Assisted Living Home, Jeffrey Hiett, Pleads Guilty to Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Hiett and his assisted living home company overbilled Medicaid $177,722.22 for services to which he was not entitled and accepted a Medicaid client he could not adequately care for due to insufficient staffing.

title: Alive Hospice Agreed to Pay $67,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Alive Hospice self-disclosed that it submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed nurse and agreed to pay $67,714.74.

title: The State of Mississippi to University of Mississippi Medical Center Agreed to Pay $368,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: UMMC employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Nurse Practitioner Sentenced to 18 Months and Ordered to Pay over $160,000 in Restitution for Health Care Fraud and Unlawful Drug Distribution
scheme: A psychiatric nurse practitioner submitted false and fraudulent claims to health care benefit programs for psychotherapy and evaluation and management services she never provided, issued 108 amphetamine prescriptions for non-medical purposes, and used Provider Relief Funds for impermissible purposes.

title: Former State Representative Pleads Guilty to Offenses Related to Cancelled State Audit of Medicaid Provider, Bank Fraud
scheme: Ziogas paid bribes to a senior state official to interfere with and cancel a Department of Social Services audit of his fiancee's Medicaid overbilling by her optometry practice, made a false statement to federal agents, and separately committed bank fraud by negotiating a $5,500 check from a client trust.

title: Adult residential group homes operator settles healthcare fraud claims
scheme: Sola, Inc. billed Virginia Medicaid for skilled and other nursing services for its group home residents that exceeded the total number of hours worked by its nurses as reported on nurses' time sheets.

title: Chicago Chiropractor Sentenced to Nearly Six Years in Prison for $2.1 Million Healthcare Fraud
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Illinois, Northern
scheme: Brown submitted more than 6,000 fraudulent claims to Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois for health care services that were not actually provided, including services purportedly provided while he was on international vacations or while his medical license was suspended.

title: Indiana Laboratory Company Agrees to Pay More Than $9 Million to Settle Alleged False Claims Act Violations
scheme: PCL knowingly submitted claims to Medicare for respiratory pathogen panels that were either medically unnecessary or obtained through kickbacks, and paid commissions to independent sales representatives and marketing firms based on the volume or value of referrals.

title: Michigan Pharmacist Sentenced to 46 Months in Prison for $4M Health Care Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Fakih billed Medicare for prescription medications, such as blood thinners and lung disease inhalers, that he did not dispense at the pharmacy he owned and operated, concealing the fraud by manipulating inventory purchases and diverting proceeds for personal use.

title: New Jersey Pharmacy Owner Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud Scheme Involving Billing Medicare for Undispensed Medication
scheme: Through a pharmacy he owned, Jaime submitted hundreds of false claims to Medicare for the medication Dificid that the pharmacy never purchased or dispensed and that beneficiaries were never prescribed, using providers' unique provider numbers on the claims.

title: Missouri Home Health Care Company Agrees to Pay $534,475 False Claims Act Settlement
scheme: The company submitted Medicaid claims on behalf of a contractor/employee who inflated his educational credentials, was not qualified to provide applied behavior analysis therapy, and billed more than 24 hours of service in a single day.

title: Southern Colorado Hospital and Doctors Agree to Pay $650,000 to Resolve Allegations That They Unlawfully Prescribed Opioids and Other Controlled Substances
scheme: Three physicians employed by Mt. San Rafael Hospital allegedly issued invalid prescriptions for controlled substances including opioids not for a legitimate medical purpose or outside the usual course of professional practice, and caused claims for those prescriptions to be submitted to Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Federal Jury Finds Markita Barnes Guilty of Healthcare Fraud, Aggravated Identity Theft, Providing Unlawful Kickbacks, Obstruction, and Money Laundering
scheme: Barnes and her employees recruited pregnant women and young mothers into her prenatal care coordination company with cash enrollment bonuses and free baby items, then used the women's personal information to submit Medicaid claims for services that were never provided, including backdated claims.

title: Pharmacist and Brother Sentenced to Prison for $15M Health Care and Wire Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: A pharmacist and his brother, a pharmacy manager, billed Medicare, Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan for prescription medications that they did not dispense at pharmacies they owned or operated, targeting expensive medications and concealing inventory shortages from auditors.

title: Vohra Wound Physicians and its Owner Agree to Pay $45M to Settle Fraud Allegations of Overbilling for Wound Care Services
scheme: Dr. Ameet Vohra and his companies knowingly caused the submission of claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary surgical procedures, for more lucrative surgical procedures when only routine non-surgical wound management had been done, and for evaluation and management services that were not billable under Medicare coverage and coding rules.

title: U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller Highlights a Dozen Significant Prosecutions During Government Shutdown
district: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), National Security Division (NSD), USAO - Louisiana, Western
scheme: Riggins paid for doctors' orders for medically unnecessary durable medical equipment and tricked doctors into signing DME orders and certificates of medical necessity, submitting over $3.8 million in fraudulent claims to Medicare and being reimbursed over $1.8 million.

title: U.K. Citizen Indicted for $2.7M Telehealth Scheme
scheme: Harrison, the beneficial owner and manager of telemedicine company CTD Network LLC, directed the company to bill Medicare more than $2.7 million for telehealth services associated with genetic testing prescriptions that were medically unnecessary and/or not provided as billed, and caused the submission of false Medicare enrollment documents.

title: Rashid Pervez, MD and North Central Ohio Health Care Agreed to Pay $698,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Bundled Services that Included Drugs that Were Not Purchased
scheme: Dr. Pervez and NCOHC submitted claims to Medicare Part B, Medicare Part C, and Ohio Medicaid for the provision and administration of Spravato under HCPCS Codes G2082 and G2083 when they did not purchase the Spravato, which was instead delivered by specialty pharmacies that billed Medicare Part D and Medicaid.

title: Justice Department Secures Denaturalization of Health Care Fraudster
scheme: Briceno owned three purported medical clinics that paid Medicare beneficiaries to undergo unnecessary tests and procedures and submitted approximately $5,460,323 in fraudulent claims to Medicare, and she concealed the fraud to obtain U.S. citizenship, which was revoked.

title: Physician Convicted of Conspiracy to Defraud Medicare
scheme: Lee, co-owner of and medical advisor to a diagnostic laboratory, conspired with others to procure genetic testing orders in exchange for kickbacks, including through purported telemedicine, causing over $24 million in false claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary genetic testing.

title: Texas Businessman Admits $1.9 Million COVID Test Kit Fraud
scheme: Companies owned by Rashid Naqvi fraudulently submitted thousands of claims to Medicare for COVID-19 test kits, obtaining $1,974,479 from roughly March 2023 to at least October 2023.

title: Attorney General Raoul Charges Cook County Physician For More Than $1 Million In Medicaid, Medicare Fraud
scheme: Khamis, a physician who owned and operated four private medical practices and four pharmacies, allegedly billed Medicaid and Medicare over $1 million for medical services and prescriptions provided by an unlicensed student from a non-certified medical school while Khamis was out of the country.

title: Physician Convicted of Conspiracy to Defraud Medicare
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Lee, co-owner and medical advisor to a diagnostic laboratory, conspired to procure genetic testing orders in exchange for kickbacks, including through purported telemedicine, and caused over $24 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary genetic testing.

title: Verde Valley Ambulance Company Agreed to Pay $40,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Rendered by an Individual that Lacked Proper Credentials
scheme: After self-disclosing, Verde Valley Ambulance Company agreed to pay $40,058.15 for allegedly billing Federal health care programs for the services of a paramedic who did not possess the appropriate Arizona state certification.

title: Mississippi Businessman Pleads Guilty to $19M Health Care Fraud Conspiracy
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Mississippi, Southern
scheme: Gibbs paid kickbacks for fraudulent doctors' orders and used them to bill Medicare over $19 million for medically unnecessary orthotic braces through seven durable medical equipment supply companies he owned or controlled, sometimes through straw owners.

title: Michael Lesem, MD and Michael D. Lesem, MD PA Agreed to Pay $546,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Bundled Services that Included Drugs that Were Not Purchased
scheme: Dr. Lesem and Lesem MD PA submitted claims to Medicare Part B and Medicare Part C for the provision and administration of Spravato under HCPCS Codes G2082 and G2083 when they did not purchase the Spravato, which was instead delivered by specialty pharmacies that billed Medicare Part D.

title: Diagnostic Laboratory Agrees to Pay More Than $1 Million to Settle Alleged False Claims Act Violations
scheme: GTI agreed to pay $1.635 million to resolve allegations that it submitted Medicare claims for respiratory pathogen panels that were medically unnecessary or obtained through kickbacks paid under a marketing services agreement with an infection prevention company for laboratory test referrals from long-term care facilities.

title: Justice Department Secures Denaturalization of Health Care Fraudster
scheme: Briceno owned three purported medical clinics that paid Medicare beneficiaries to undergo unnecessary tests and procedures and submitted approximately $5,460,323 in fraudulent claims to Medicare, and she later concealed the fraud to obtain U.S. citizenship, which was revoked.

title: Missouri Man Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for $174 Million Health Care Fraud Conspiracy
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Louisiana, Eastern
scheme: McNamara operated laboratories that billed Medicare for cancer and cardiovascular genetic testing obtained through telemarketing and purported telemedicine doctors' orders procured with kickbacks, shifted billing between labs, and concealed his ownership by listing family members as owners.

title: Little Rock Psychologist Indicted by Federal Grand Jury for Defrauding Medicare and Arkansas Blue Cross Blue Shield
scheme: Banks billed Medicare and Arkansas Blue Cross and Blue Shield for thousands of hours of psychotherapy services that never took place, including sessions for patients seen only once and patients who had died, and created fictitious records to conceal the billing.

title: Founder/CEO and Clinical President of Digital Health Company Convicted in $100M Adderall Distribution and Health Care Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), USAO - California, Northern
scheme: He and Brody used the digital health company Done to distribute Adderall and other stimulants over the internet in exchange for monthly subscription fees and submitted false prior authorization requests and claims to Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurers.

title: Founder/CEO And Clinical President Of Digital Health Company Convicted In $100m Adderall Distribution And Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: He and Brody used the digital health company Done to distribute Adderall and other stimulants over the internet in exchange for monthly subscription fees and submitted false prior authorization requests and claims to insurers, resulting in payments in excess of approximately $14 million.

title: Connecticut Dentists Pay More than $714K to Settle False Claims Allegations
scheme: Two dental practices and their owners paid a third-party patient recruiting company a fee for each Connecticut Medicaid patient referred and submitted claims for those patients to the Connecticut Medical Assistance Program while impliedly certifying that no kickbacks were paid.

title: Florida Man Indicted for Health Care Fraud, Wire Fraud in Durable Medical Equipment Scheme
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - South Carolina
scheme: Weinberger, who was excluded from Medicare, allegedly concealed his ownership and control of a Medicare-enrolled durable medical equipment company through a false enrollment document and, with coconspirators, used call centers to generate doctors' orders for orthotic braces and submit approximately $6.7 million in false and fraudulent claims obtained through kickbacks and bribes, medically unnecessary, or otherwise ineligible for reimbursement.

title: AG’s Office Secures Guilty Plea From Dracut Physician Charged With Involuntary Manslaughter And Illegally Prescribing Opioids
scheme: A physician pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter for illegally prescribing opioids to at-risk patients, resulting in one patient's death, and to defrauding MassHealth, the state's Medicaid program.

title: Memphis Doctor to Pay $375,296.90 to Settle Fraudulent Billing Allegations
scheme: A Memphis nephrologist was alleged to have falsely billed Medicare for end-stage renal disease treatment visits to dialysis patients that he never actually performed.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces 2 Convictions and an Arrest Made by His Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
scheme: Two caregivers were convicted of Medicaid fraud for billing for services not provided and a third was arrested and charged after electronic visit verification records showed she was not at beneficiary residences when she reported delivering in-home personal care.

title: Anchorage Doctor and Husband Plead Guilty to Multi-Million Dollar Health Care, Tax Fraud Schemes
scheme: An Anchorage rheumatologist and her husband underdosed patients, injected free samples, expired, or different medications, and billed more than 10 insurance plans for 4,829 units of medication despite purchasing only 369 units, and overstated clinic expenses on tax returns.

title: Corporation and Former Chief Executive Officer Sentenced for Health Care Fraud and Tax Conspiracy
district: Civil Division, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Wisconsin, Western
scheme: The defendants diverted CMS funds intended for the operation and care of residents at 23 Wisconsin skilled nursing facilities for personal expenses and owner distributions, failed to disclose this to CMS, diverted employee health insurance premiums and 401(k) contributions and resident account money, and directed that withheld employment taxes not be paid to the IRS.

title: Nine Medicaid Providers Facing Fraud Charges
scheme: Nine Medicaid providers were indicted for billing Medicaid for in-home services not provided, including billing while clients were hospitalized, inflating service hours, sending unqualified individuals to provide care, and forging a client's signature on timesheets.

title: Four California Residents Sentenced to Prison in Connection with $16M Hospice Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - California, Central
scheme: Defendants operated four sham hospice companies that billed Medicare nearly $16 million for hospice services that were medically unnecessary and never provided, used foreign nationals' identities as straw owners, and laundered the proceeds through shell company accounts.

title: Strata Pathology Services Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Improper Remuneration in the Form of Free Access to Systems
scheme: Strata paid remuneration to a physician practice in the form of free access to its Laboratory Information Systems that the physician practice used for reporting the practice's professional component of histopathology testing.

title: Coeur d’Alene Physician Found Guilty in Telemarketing Medicare Fraud Conspiracy
scheme: A physician signed false and fraudulent orders for genetic tests and durable medical equipment braces for Medicare beneficiaries he never contacted, using prescriptions generated by a telemarketing company that sold them to labs and DME companies that billed Medicare.

title: Tri-Cities Urgent Care Clinic Agrees to Pay $2.8 Million to Resolve Claims of Overbilling for Diagnostic Tests
scheme: Health First Urgent Care allegedly unbundled PCR respiratory and urinary tract infection panel tests and billed for each individual test, and billed for more expensive panel tests that were not medically necessary.

title: President of Insurance Brokerage Firm and CEO of Marketing Company Convicted in $233M Affordable Care Act Enrollment Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Lloyd and Strong submitted false and fraudulent applications to enroll low-income consumers in fully subsidized Affordable Care Act plans for which they were ineligible, seeking over $233 million in subsidies, in order to obtain commission payments from insurance companies.

title: Aesculap Implant Systems Agrees to Pay $38.5 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations Related to Knee Implant Failures
scheme: Aesculap sold knee replacement devices that it knew would fail prematurely at a higher than acceptable rate, resulting in false claims to Medicare and Medicaid, and paid unlawful remuneration to a physician to induce him to use the knee implants.

title: CVS Pharmacy Inc. Pays $18.2 Million to Resolve Alleged False Claims Act Violations
scheme: CVS submitted pharmacy claims to California's Medi-Cal program between 2010 and 2021 using false electronic certifications that patients had qualifying medical conditions, without verifying or documenting applicable diagnosis and documentation requirements.

title: VRA Enterprises Agrees To Pay Over $17 Million For Allegedly Billing Medicare For Over-The-Counter COVID-19 Tests That Were Not Provided To Beneficiaries, Or That Were Sent To Beneficiaries Months After Being Billed To Medicare
scheme: VRA Enterprises agreed to pay the United States to resolve allegations it submitted false claims to Medicare for over-the-counter COVID-19 tests that were not provided to beneficiaries or were shipped months after being billed.

title: Diagnostic Laboratory Agrees To Pay More Than $9 Million To Settle Alleged False Claims Act Violations
scheme: Patients Choice Laboratories agreed to pay the United States $9,620,000 to resolve allegations that it violated the False Claims Act and the Anti-Kickback Statute.

title: Baltimore County Woman Sentenced for Impersonating Nurses and Aggravated Identity Theft
scheme: Amponsah used stolen nursing licenses and false educational and professional histories to obtain employment as a purported licensed nurse at no less than 40 facilities in Maryland that billed health care benefit programs including Medicare and Medicaid for services she provided, earning more than $145,000 in wages.

title: Alabama Doctor Pleads Guilty to $6 Million Telemedicine Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Robinson worked with telemedicine companies to sign pre-populated orders for medically unnecessary durable medical equipment and genetic testing for Medicare beneficiaries he did not contact, resulting in over $6 million in claims submitted to Medicare.

title: ICYMI: Charges, Pleas, Sentencings And Settlements During The Recent Government Shutdown
scheme: Johnika Davis and Jimmie Moorehead were indicted for conspiracy and false statements related to health care matters for falsely claiming physical disabilities and need for Medicaid-funded personal care services in exchange for kickbacks from a co-conspirator, and separately Angela K. Williams pleaded guilty to identity theft for seeking employment on the medical staff of the Choctaw Nation Health Services Authority using a St. Louis doctor's stolen identity and forged credentials.

title: Iowa Attorney Pleads Guilty to Making a False Statement to Iowa Medicaid
scheme: An attorney submitted documents to Iowa Medicaid to qualify an elderly client for nursing home benefits, including a statement that a 1961 Rolls Royce had a fair market value of $194,000 when he knew it did not.

title: Telemarketing Company Operators Sentenced For Roles In Genetic Testing Fraud Scheme
scheme: Two operators of a marketing company solicited Medicare beneficiaries for medically unnecessary genetic testing, and one also falsified ownership information in Medicare enrollment documentation for a clinical laboratory.

title: San Antonio Regional Hospital Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Improper Remuneration in the Form of Free Prior Authorization Services
scheme: OIG alleged that San Antonio Regional Hospital paid remuneration to doctors in the form of free prior authorization services not provided to other physicians.

title: Telemarketing Company Operators Sentenced for Roles in Genetic Testing Fraud Scheme
scheme: Two operators of a telemarketing company recruited Medicare beneficiaries for medically unnecessary cancer genetic testing and received kickbacks for referrals, and one of them also enrolled a clinical laboratory in Medicare using other people's identities to disguise his ownership.

title: William Mangan, DO Agreed to Excluded for 10 Years for Allegedly Submitting Claims for Unnecessary Genetic Tests and DMEPOS
scheme: Dr. Mangan worked for a purported telemedicine company and ordered genetic tests and DMEPOS that were not reasonable or necessary, falsely certifying that he had evaluated the patients and that the orders were medically necessary.

title: Spartanburg Medical Center Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Inappropriately Transferring a Patient
scheme: OIG concluded that in May 2024 Spartanburg Medical Center inappropriately transferred a patient to another hospital instead of providing stabilizing treatment for the patient's emergency medical condition, in violation of EMTALA.

title: Business Owner Sentenced to More Than Five Years in Prison for Fraud and Money Laundering Schemes
scheme: Yeghiazaryan committed fraud offenses targeting government programs using shell companies and false identities, including participating in a scheme to defraud Medicaid and pandemic relief programs, and money laundering.

title: Blick Center Agreed to Pay $165,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Psychotherapy Services that Were Not Provided as Billed
scheme: Blick Center billed Federal health care programs for psychotherapy services by an employed licensed clinical social worker that were not provided as billed.

title: Genesis Behavioral Services Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Improper Remuneration in Exchange for Referrals
scheme: Genesis paid remuneration to Qualified Behavioral Health Specialists in return for recruiting new QBHSs who referred their clients to Genesis for mental health outpatient treatment services, some of which were paid for in whole or in part by Medicare and Medicaid.

title: AG's Office Secures $175,000 from Fall River Pediatrician for Submitting False Claims to MassHealth
scheme: Dr. Tural submitted false claims for services he purportedly provided to MassHealth members that were actually provided by midlevel practitioners such as physician assistants and certified nurse practitioners.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces 2 Arrests for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Troup, an aide for a personal care agency, billed for services by clocking in and out of shifts at Henry's residence while she was working at the Arkansas Department of Corrections, and the two shared the proceeds.

title: Delta County Woman Pleads Guilty to Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Stouffer submitted logs purportedly verifying home help work by a family member she selected as her provider from November 2021 through August 2022, and received approximately $8,000 in payments for services the family member denied providing.

title: Attorney General’s Medicaid Fraud and Vulnerable Victims Unit Secures a $200,000 Settlement and Corporate Oversight of Patapsco Healthcare
scheme: Patapsco Healthcare settled allegations that it violated the Maryland False Health Claims Act by providing substandard care to Medicaid residents, including wound care inadequacies, inadequate nutrition and hydration, regulatory violations, preventable falls, and failure to prevent opiate overdoses.

title: Hopebridge Agreed to Pay $25,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Without Proper Treatment Plans
scheme: Hopebridge self-disclosed and OIG alleged that it submitted claims for plans of care that were not individualized to the patient.

title: Exact Sciences Laboratories Agreed to Pay $85,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: After self-disclosing, Exact Sciences Laboratories agreed to pay $85,139.39 for allegedly employing an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Affiliated Pharmacies To Pay More Than $150,000 For False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Multiple Oklahoma pharmacies agreed to pay $157,000 to settle allegations that they billed the Oklahoma Medicaid Program, SoonerCare, for hundreds of unauthorized over-the-counter COVID-19 tests.

title: Metropolis Dermatology Agreed to Pay $140,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Incident-to Services Not Covered
scheme: Metropolis Dermatology submitted claims for "incident to" services that did not satisfy the "incident to" requirements because they were provided during initial visits with new patients or during visits with existing patients during which a new plan of care was established, and some were provided by providers not yet enrolled at the time of service.

title: Indianapolis man charged with 43 counts of Medicaid fraud after billing for more than $2.7 million
scheme: He allegedly falsified documents to indicate a qualified physician was overseeing mental health services at TRUTH Treatment Centers Inc. and submitted bills totaling more than $2.7 million for addiction treatment services purportedly provided by medical professionals, when counseling was provided by recent graduates of its drug treatment program without required education and licensure.

title: Oregon DOJ Successfully Places Private Care Agency on Probation in Medicaid Fraud Case
scheme: Rever Grand, Inc. entered a no-contest plea to one count of Making a False Claim for Health Care Payment, and its founder and his wife are alleged to have used the agency to funnel Medicaid funds to themselves.

title: Swedish Medical Center and Swedish Medical Group Agreed to Pay $10 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided for in Clinical Research Studies
scheme: OIG alleged that Swedish submitted claims to Federal health care programs for items and services provided in inpatient and outpatient focused clinical research studies that should have been paid for by the research study sponsor or provided free to the research participant.

title: ONE Health Ohio Agreed to Pay $24,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services that Did Not Meet the Requirements of Time-Based Codes
scheme: ONE submitted false claims to Medicare and Medicaid for individual psychotherapy services purportedly rendered using CPT Code 90832 that were not performed for the minimum duration required by this time-based code.

title: Lee Health System Agreed to Pay $18.8 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing Excluded Individuals and Submitting Claims for Services that Were Not Performed or Failed to Meet Coverage Criteria
scheme: Lee Health employed two individuals it knew or should have known were excluded from Federal health care programs and submitted claims for transcatheter aortic valve replacement procedures that were not performed or failed to meet coverage criteria.

title: Repeat Offender Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud Scheme in New Hampshire
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - New Hampshire
scheme: Alonso, an excluded psychotherapist, worked for a New Hampshire telehealth mental health provider and caused claims to be submitted to New Hampshire Medicaid for services he was barred from billing and for counseling services that were not provided as represented, causing payments of approximately $173,998.83.

title: Two Plead Guilty To Medicaid Fraud In Case Attorney General Ellison Investigated Jointly With U.S. Attorney’s Office
scheme: Evergreen Recovery leaders overbilled DHS and UCare for substance abuse treatment services they did not deliver, falsified and back-dated records, and steered clients to a sober housing provider controlled by an Evergreen owner in exchange for attending billable programming.

title: Four more charged in $110 million hospice fraud scheme
scheme: Seven defendants conspired to fraudulently bill Medicare and Medicaid for more than $110 million for hospice services provided to patients who were not terminally ill, paying kickbacks for referrals and laundering reimbursements through straw-owned successor hospice companies.

title: Gastroenterology Group of Rochester Agreed to Pay $352,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting False Evaluation and Management Claims
scheme: GGR submitted claims to Federal health care programs for evaluation and management services furnished as split/shared visits between GGR physicians and hospital-employed advanced practice gastroenterology providers who were not in the same group practice, where the billing provider did not perform the substantive portion of the visit.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces 7 Arrests Made by His Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
scheme: Seven individuals, mostly caregivers, were arrested on charges including billing Medicaid for personal care services not provided, manipulating the telephonic verification system, splitting proceeds of fraudulent billing with beneficiaries' families, and exploitation of a vulnerable person.

title: Eight Medicaid Providers Indicted, Accused of Phantom Billing
scheme: Seven individuals and one business were indicted for submitting Medicaid claims for services that were not provided, including billing for in-home services while clients were incarcerated, on vacation or receiving other care, a kickback scheme, and submitting fraudulent timesheets.

title: Bucks County Home Care Company and Its Owners and Managers Charged in Alleged Health Care Fraud Scheme
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Pennsylvania, Eastern
scheme: Favorite Home Care, LLC and its owners and managers billed Medicaid and a Medicaid Managed Care Organization for home health services that were not rendered, completing electronic visit verification calls attesting to providing services when they were not present with the client.

title: Eastern Nephrology Agreed to Pay $81,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Eastern Nephrology employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston Agreed to Pay $390,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Upcoded Evaluation and Management Claims
scheme: UTHSC submitted claims for evaluation and management services performed by a physician as level 4 or 5 when a lower level of service was provided, and billed for E/M services when the physician only performed a procedure during the visit with no separately identifiable, medically necessary E/M services provided.

title: Attorney General Raúl Torrez Recovers More Than $1.5 Million from Former New Mexico State Police Officer Charged in Substance Abuse Recovery Scheme
scheme: The defendants operated a now-shuttered substance abuse recovery program that billed the Medicaid program hundreds of thousands of dollars in fraudulent claims, involving identity theft, document falsification and unauthorized medical practice.

title: Fawn Gobis Sentenced for Theft and Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Gobis submitted false timesheets and documentation to a Medicaid area agency claiming her son was providing Medicaid-covered services to a recipient while he was living in Colorado, resulting in her receiving $10,998.15 in benefits.

title: Plaster’s union member sentenced for defrauding health care plan
scheme: Weatherbee submitted 12 fraudulent invoices totaling $44,012 to his union's health and welfare fund for purported out of pocket medical expenses, converting the funds for his own use.

title: Compounding Pharmacy Owner Sent Back to Prison
scheme: Compounding pharmacy owner previously convicted of conspiracy to offer and pay health care kickbacks was sentenced for violating supervised release by failing to make restitution payments and concealing accounts, businesses, and asset transfers from Probation.

title: TennCare Fraud Investigation Leads to Arrest of Former Shelby County Home Care Operator
scheme: The former operator of a home healthcare agency knowingly billed TennCare for home healthcare related services for patients who were receiving treatment in area hospitals from July 2018 through August 2021.

title: S&G Staffing and Jacobs Marketing Agreed to Be Excluded for 10 Years for Receiving Improper Remuneration
scheme: S&G Staffing and Jacobs Marketing participated in a scheme to pay kickbacks disguised as purported management services organization distribution payments to doctors to induce the doctors to send their laboratory testing referrals to a critical access hospital that funded the kickbacks.

title: Three Charged with Medicaid Fraud in Alleged Transportation Scheme
scheme: Three Medicaid beneficiaries allegedly used a location-spoofing app to trick a mileage-tracking phone app and submitted mileage reimbursement requests to the Michigan Medicaid transportation program for trips that never took place.

title: Attorney General Hanaway Secures Felony Indictments In Four Major Medicaid Fraud Cases In St. Louis
scheme: A Cole County grand jury indicted four sets of defendants in the St. Louis region for submitting false nursing reports, billing the maximum hours from care plans without time records, and billing for in-home personal care services not rendered, totaling more than $230,000 in Medicaid claims.

title: Highmark Agreed to Pay $71,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Highmark employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Attorney General Alan Wilson announces arrest of Horry Co. case manager for forgery, Medicaid fraud
scheme: Between March 25, 2024, and June 27, 2024, Lerner allegedly submitted false payment claims to the South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services by falsifying case notes and quarterly review plans claiming services were provided to Medicaid beneficiaries when no such services were rendered.

title: Bethel Psychologist Charged with Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Vaillancourt submitted claims for payment to Vermont Medicaid for psychotherapy sessions he had not provided and failed to maintain patient records as required.

title: AG Sunday: Philadelphia Pharmacy Pleads Guilty, Will Pay $2.3M Restitution for Medicaid Fraud Scheme Involving Unregulated HIV Meds
scheme: A pharmacy dispensed an estimated 100,000 HIV medication tablets that were not obtained from legitimate wholesale suppliers and billed Medicaid and Medicare for reimbursement.

title: Clinic owner arrested in multimillion-dollar fraud scheme involving non-existent psychotherapy services
scheme: Spears allegedly submitted approximately $4 million in false Medicare claims for psychotherapy services that were never provided, billing under the names of seven licensed clinical social workers after they resigned and for beneficiaries who were deceased at the time of the billed treatment.

title: Symphony Crestwood, Symphony Chicago West, and Symphony Midway Agreed to Pay $107,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Symphony employed an individual excluded from Federal health care programs who worked as a licensed practical nurse and provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: AccuCare Home Health Services Agreed to Pay $20,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: AccuCare employed an individual excluded from participating in any Federal health care program who worked as a home health aide and provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Semler Scientific Inc. and Bard Peripheral Vascular Inc. to Pay Nearly $37 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations Relating to FloChec and QuantaFlo Devices
scheme: Semler Scientific Inc. and its former distributor Bard Peripheral Vascular Inc. agreed to pay to resolve allegations that they knowingly caused, and conspired to cause, the submission of false claims to Medicare for photoplethysmography tests performed using the FloChec and QuantaFlo devices in connection with the diagnosis of peripheral arterial disease.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces Conviction of Little Rock Woman for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Burt was a caregiver who claimed to provide services to a Medicaid beneficiary while the beneficiary was a patient in a hospital, but those services were never provided.

title: Owner of Mail Order Pharmacies Settles False Claims Act Investigation Involving Allegations of Fraudulent Billing Practices and Kickbacks
scheme: An Orange County, California resident who owned mail order pharmacies settled allegations that he violated the False Claims Act by paying kickbacks in exchange for the referral of certain prescriptions.

title: Semler Scientific Inc. And Bard Peripheral Vascular Inc. To Pay Nearly $37M To Resolve False Claims Act Allegations Relating To Flochec And Quantaflo Devices
scheme: Semler and Bard knowingly caused and conspired to cause healthcare providers to submit false claims to Medicare for photoplethysmography tests performed with the FloChec and QuantaFlo devices by representing that the tests were reimbursable under CPT codes 93922, 93923 and 93924 even though the devices do not perform an ankle brachial index.

title: University of Mississippi Medical Center Agreed to Pay $271,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that UMMC submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed registered nurse.

title: Attorney General Alan Wilson Announces Rock Hill Counselor Charged With Medicaid Fraud
scheme: A Licensed Professional Counselor employed by a South Carolina Medicaid provider allegedly prepared and submitted falsified timesheets and fraudulent payment claims exceeding $10,000 to the South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services for behavioral health services to minor Medicaid beneficiaries that were not rendered.

title: David Boguslavsky, MD and Premier Medical Acupuncture Agreed to Pay $581,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Bundled Services that Included Drugs that Were Not Purchased
scheme: Dr. Boguslavsky and Premier submitted claims to Medicare Part B, Medicare Part C, and Medicaid for the provision and administration of Spravato under HCPCS Codes G2082 and G2083 when they did not purchase the Spravato, which specialty pharmacies delivered to Premier and billed to Medicare Part D and Medicaid.

title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Announces $3 Million Settlement Agreement With Gilead Sciences To Resolve Improper Promotion Of HIV Drugs
scheme: Gilead Sciences allegedly offered and paid remuneration in the form of payments, meals, and travel expenses to health care practitioners who spoke at or attended Gilead speaker events to encourage them to prescribe Gilead HIV drugs between January 2011 and November 2017, causing false claims to be submitted to the Florida Medicaid program.

title: First Defendant Charged in Autism Fraud Scheme
scheme: Hassan and others enrolled Smart Therapy LLC as an EIDBI autism services provider, recruited children with cash kickbacks to parents, employed unqualified behavioral technicians, and submitted inflated and fabricated Medicaid claims for services not provided, obtaining more than $14 million, while also submitting approximately $465,000 in fraudulent Federal Child Nutrition Program claims through Feeding Our Future.

title: Tri-Cities Urgent Care Clinic Agrees to Pay $2.8 Million to Resolve Claims of Overbilling for Diagnostic Tests
scheme: Health First Urgent Care allegedly unbundled PCR respiratory and urinary tract infection panel tests and billed for each individual test, and billed for more expensive panel tests that were not medically necessary, resulting in overbilling to Medicare and Medicaid.

title: Reno Doctor Arrested And Indicted For Health Care Fraud
scheme: An OB-GYN allegedly submitted false claims to Medicaid and private health plans for gynecologic tests and surgical procedures that were not medically necessary and falsified patients' medical records.

title: Attorney General Ellison Partners With Federal Law Enforcement In Medicaid Fraud Charges Against Asha Hassan
scheme: Hassan used her EIDBI agency Smart Therapy to bill Medicaid for autism services not rendered at all, services that were inflated, and services rendered only because parents received kickbacks for their child receiving services through Smart Therapy.

title: Justice Department Expands Health Care Fraud Unit to Target Health Care Fraud in Massachusetts
scheme: The Justice Department announced the expansion of its Health Care Fraud Unit's New England Strike Force to the District of Massachusetts to investigate and prosecute health care fraud schemes.

title: Physician Sentenced to 14 Years for Illegal Distribution of Opioids and Health Care Fraud Conspiracies
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Anand conspired to submit false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, OPM, Independence Blue Cross, and Anthem for "Goody Bags" of medically unnecessary prescription medications dispensed by his in-house pharmacies, and conspired to distribute oxycodone outside the usual course of medical practice, including prescriptions written by unlicensed medical interns on pre-signed blank prescriptions.

title: Keith Myers Agreed to Pay $250,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Causing False Claims, Records, and Statements Related to Federally Funded COVID-19 Vaccines
scheme: Myers, as CEO of MorseLife Health System Inc., caused MorseLife to request COVID-19 vaccine shots funded by the CDC's Pharmacy Partnership for Long-Term Care Program to vaccinate individuals who were neither residents nor staff of MorseLife and were ineligible under the program, with false representations made to the administering pharmacy.

title: Essex County Man Charged with Submitting Thousands of False Bills to Medicaid, Stealing More than $3 Million
scheme: Lopez allegedly billed or directed employees to bill Medicaid for over 34,000 claims for psychological services under a licensed psychiatrist's provider name and number without permission, including for canceled or no-show appointments and for case management services, receiving approximately $3.4 million although neither he nor JLA were approved Medicaid providers, and failed to pay taxes for 2021-2023.

title: Fresno County Podiatrist and Sales Representative Plead Guilty to Conspiracy to Submit False Claims Related to Skin Grafts
scheme: A podiatrist purchased skin grafts from a sales representative and allowed him, an unlicensed person, to apply them to Medicare and Medi-Cal beneficiaries, then submitted claims falsely representing that the podiatrist had applied the grafts.

title: Marketer Sentenced for $11.5M Genetic Testing Fraud and Kickback Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Desselle and co-conspirators convinced Medicare beneficiaries to take unnecessary genetic tests, paid marketers to recruit beneficiaries, bribed a telemedicine company for doctors' orders, and received kickbacks from clinical laboratories that billed Medicare $11.5 million.

title: SMP Health St. Raphael Agreed to Pay $233,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that SMP employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Our Community Pharmacy and Candida Webb Agreed to Pay $100,000 and Be Excluded for 5 Years for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Remuneration to Beneficiaries
scheme: OCP and Webb paid remuneration to a customer in the form of cash on two separate occasions to induce the customer to purchase drugs payable by Medicare from OCP.

title: Weirton Medical Center Agreed to Pay $54,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Weirton Medical Center self-disclosed that it employed an individual it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Hiawatha Care Center Agreed to Pay $201,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Hiawatha Care Center self-disclosed that it employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Defendants Charged in First Wave of Housing Stabilization Fraud Cases
scheme: Eight defendants were federally charged with wire fraud for their roles in a housing stabilization fraud scheme.

title: United States Files Lawsuit Against San Bernardino County-Based Health Plan for Alleged False Claims to California’s Medicaid Program
scheme: The United States alleges IEHP misused surplus Medi-Cal Expansion funding through sham incentive programs and an extra-contractual retroactive rate increase, made false statements about the nature, timing, and purpose of payments to providers, and knowingly retained overpayments.

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Seeks Potential Victims in Case Against St. Louis Doctor and Staff
scheme: The indictment alleges the three conspired to prescribe controlled substances outside the usual course of professional practice and that Parks and Bilderback conspired to defraud Medicare, Missouri Medicaid and private health insurers by billing claims that falsely identified Parks as the provider, including when he was out of the country.

title: United States Files Suit Against California-Based Health Plan for Alleged False Claims to California’s Medicaid Program
scheme: The United States alleges IEHP made false statements to Medi-Cal about the nature, timing, and purpose of payments to providers and knowingly retained overpayments by misspending Medi-Cal Expansion funding through sham incentive programs and an extra-contractual retroactive rate increase.

title: Two Florida Men Charged for $34.8M Fraud Scheme Targeting Medicare Beneficiaries
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Two men who owned and operated seven Florida durable medical equipment supply companies allegedly paid kickbacks to marketing companies that used deceptive telemarketing and telemedicine-generated doctors' orders to submit approximately $34.8 million in false claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary orthotic braces and continuous glucose monitors.

title: Exactech Agrees to Pay $8 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations for Selling Defective Knee Implant Devices
scheme: Exactech allegedly violated the False Claims Act by knowingly submitting or causing the submission of false claims for payment to Medicare, Medicaid, and the Department of Veterans Affairs in connection with defective knee-replacement devices.

title: Three More Plead Guilty In 1st Adult N Pediatric Healthcare Fraud Case
scheme: Owners and employees of a Medicaid-enrolled home health agency conspired to submit false claims to Medicaid for nursing and personal care services that were not provided, including paying patients' family members for blank signed nursing notes that were filled out to support the claims.

title: U.S. Attorney's Office Collects $48 Million Restitution Ordered Against Insys Executives Convicted of Health Care Racketeering Conspiracy
scheme: Insys Therapeutics' founder and six former executives conspired to bribe medical practitioners to prescribe the fentanyl spray Subsys, often when medically unnecessary, and to mislead health insurance providers and Medicare to obtain payment for the drug.

title: Suburban Chicago Man Indicted on Federal Healthcare Fraud Charges
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Illinois, Northern
scheme: Bashir created fictitious entities called Success for Kids and Growing Kids Therapy and submitted approximately $17.3 million in false claims to a private insurer for early intervention therapy services that were not provided, causing at least $1.4 million in payments.

title: Roanoke Home Health Care Attendant Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud
scheme: Dowdy submitted fraudulent timesheets and billed Medicaid for 1,970.5 hours of personal home health care and respite services that were not rendered to two Medicaid recipients.

title: Medical Device Company Exactech, Inc. Agrees to Pay $8 Million for Selling Allegedly Defective Knee Implant Devices
scheme: Exactech agreed to pay $8 million to resolve allegations that it knowingly submitted or caused the submission of false claims to Medicare, Medicaid, and the Department of Veterans Affairs in connection with defective knee replacement devices.

title: Georgia Man Sentenced to Over 4 Years in Prison for Fraud Targeting AHCCCS
scheme: Harrison concealed his ownership of a behavioral health company enrolled as an AHCCCS provider and billed AHCCCS for counseling services that were never provided to enrollees.

title: AG Campbell Secures Guilty Plea From Ringleader Of Worcester-Based Home Health Fraud Scheme Exploiting Vulnerable Residents
scheme: Mercedes and co-conspirators stole personal information from disabled, elderly, and unhoused individuals and billed MassHealth over $500,000 for home health services that were never provided, including PCA, HHA, and AFC program services.

title: Attorney General Ellison partners with federal law enforcement on indictments of Housing Stabilization Services providers
scheme: Principals of four Housing Stabilization Services agencies billed Minnesota's Medical Assistance program for HSS services that were not delivered, often billing the maximum authorized amount while delivering minimal or no services.

title: Federal Jury Finds Former Prenatal Care Coordinator Guilty of Healthcare Fraud, Aggravated Identity Theft, Providing Unlawful Kickbacks, and Money Laundering
scheme: Cruse lured pregnant women and young mothers into her prenatal care coordination company with kickbacks of free baby items and then used their personal information to submit Medicaid claims for services that were never provided.

title: FORMER HOME HEALTH CARE OPERATOR SETTLES FRAUD ALLEGATIONS OF BILLING FEDERAL HEALTH CARE PROGRAMS FOR SERVICES PERFORMED BY UNLICENSED FOREIGN DOCTORS
scheme: Irene Oshiyoye submitted, or caused the submission of, false claims by Advance Visiting Physicians to Medicare and Medicaid for home health visits performed by unlicensed and unsupervised foreign doctors.

title: Louisiana Chiropractor Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison for Health Care Fraud and Unemployment Insurance Fraud Schemes
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: A chiropractor billed Blue Cross Blue Shield of Louisiana for uncovered massages and for chiropractic services that were not performed or not performed as billed, including while he was out of the office, fabricated patient records during an audit, and falsely certified unemployment to obtain pandemic unemployment benefits.

title: Arizona’s Children Association Agreed to Pay $54,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitted Claims for Services Not Provided
scheme: After self-disclosing to OIG, Arizona's Children Association agreed to pay $54,985.86 for allegedly submitting claims for behavioral health services, such as life skills and family support, that were not provided.

title: Las Vegas Surgical Associates Agreed to Pay $20,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Ablation Procedures that Misrepresented Dates of Service or Were Upcoded
scheme: LVSA submitted claims for one of its providers that misrepresented the date(s) of service for ablation procedures, and/or upcoded claims for these services.

title: Jacksonville Fire and Rescue Department Agreed to Pay $167,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by Unlicensed Individuals
scheme: JFRD submitted claims for services provided by unlicensed paramedics and emergency medicine technicians.

title: Media Advisory- Chesapeake Regional Medical Center (CRMC) Case Updates
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: CRMC was charged with conspiracy to defraud the United States and health care fraud related to its billing to insurance companies for Dr. Javaid Perwaiz's performance of surgeries and other procedures at its facility, including unnecessary hysterectomies, elective inductions before 39 weeks without medical justification, and sterilizations of Medicaid patients without consent forms signed 30 days in advance.

title: Alexandra Tellez Agreed to Pay $60,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in Exchange for Referring Medicare Services
scheme: Tellez received remuneration in the form of monetary payments and a gift in return for referring individuals or arranging for the furnishing of items or services for which the Medicare program paid.

title: Marianjoy Rehabilitation Hospital and Clinics Agreed to Pay $190,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: MRHC self-disclosed that it submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed speech pathologist.

title: Clay County Pharmacy Investigation and Prosecution Ends in Guilty Pleas
scheme: Pharmacy owners and pharmacists dispensed large volumes of controlled substances without legitimate medical purpose, submitted false claims for medically unnecessary controlled substance combinations to Medicare Part D and TennCare, and paid kickbacks, copayments, cash, and "Monkey Bucks" to recruit and retain patients.

title: Memphis Woman Charged with Abuse of Vulnerable Adult
scheme: TBI agents determined that Jackson, a caregiver paid to provide in-home care services to a TennCare recipient, had been involved in a physical altercation with that recipient, and she was charged with Abuse of a Vulnerable Adult.

title: Maryland Woman Arraigned for Defrauding the D.C. Medicaid Program
district: Office of the Inspector General, USAO - District of Columbia
scheme: While employed by a District Mental Health Rehabilitation Service provider as a community support worker, Jalloh submitted encounter notes for community support services she did not provide and overbilled for services she allegedly provided to District Medicaid beneficiaries.

title: Florida Man Sentenced to 24 Months for Laundering Proceeds of Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Farese invested in a DME supply company involved in billing Medicare and other insurers for orthotic braces that patients did not want or need, and after learning of the arrests he received $495,000 in proceeds of the scheme into his bank account.

title: Doctor and Urgent Care Clinic Settle Allegations Over Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Family Choice Urgent Care billed Oregon Medicaid for medically unnecessary office visits and for higher levels of visits than were actually provided for asymptomatic patients.

title: Office of Attorney General’s Role in Investigating Owner of Pittsburgh Facility for Intellectually Disabled Adults Leads to Federal Plea to Health Care Fraud
scheme: Oliver-Hollis obtained authorization for increased Medicaid billing rates for residents requiring above average staffing ratios between 2018 and 2023 while almost never staffing the homes sufficiently for the residents' needs or as required by law.

title: St. Louis Area Doctor Sentenced to 70 Months in Prison
district: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Missouri, Eastern
scheme: A physician paid kickbacks for urine specimens referred to his laboratory, signed and pre-signed prescriptions for controlled substances without seeing patients or determining medical need, and billed Medicare for annual wellness visits under another doctor's name and billing number for services not performed in person.

title: Compassion Hospice Agreed to Pay $430,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Improper Remuneration in the Form of Referral Based Compensation
scheme: OIG alleged that Compassion paid remuneration to two physicians in the form of Medical Director compensation that took into account the physicians' volume or value of referrals.

title: Owners of 1st Adult N Pediatric Healthcare Pled Guilty
scheme: Owners and employees of a Medicaid-enrolled home health agency conspired to submit false claims to Medicaid for services not provided, including falsifying records and paying parents or guardians of patients for blank, signed nursing notes used to support billing.

title: Randolph Personal Care Attendant Sentenced To 18 Months In Jail For Defrauding MassHealth
scheme: Acting as a personal care attendant, she conspired with multiple individuals to cause the submission of over $150,000 in false claims to MassHealth for PCA services that were never provided.

title: Laboratory CEO, Marketers, and Physicians to Pay Over $6M to Settle Allegations of Management Service Organization and other Lab Testing Kickbacks
scheme: A former laboratory CEO, two physicians, and seven marketers agreed to pay over $6 million to resolve False Claims Act allegations of illegal payments to doctors for laboratory referrals, including kickbacks disguised as management service organization investment distributions.

title: Owner of Facility for Intellectually Disabled Adults Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud
scheme: Oliver-Hollis, an enrolled Medicaid provider operating Serenitycare LLC under Pennsylvania's Home and Community-Based Services Waiver Program, failed to sufficiently staff homes housing intellectually disabled adults and submitted weekly claims falsely representing proper staffing between 2018 and 2023.

title: Laurels of Sandy Creek and Laurel of Hudsonville Agreed to Pay $122,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that the Laurels employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Ryan Cleland, DC and Infinite Wellness Integrative Medical Center Agreed to Pay $249,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Medically Unnecessary Services
scheme: Cleland and Infinite Wellness presented and caused to be presented false and fraudulent claims to the Medicare Part B Program for electrical cell signaling treatments using electrical stimulation codes and vitamin injections that were not medically reasonable or necessary and not reimbursable by Medicare.

title: Community Memorial Health System Agreed to Pay $111,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: CMHS submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed registered nurse.

title: Opal Mullings and Optimum Faith Lab Corp. Were Excluded for 10 Years
scheme: OIG excluded Optimum Faith Lab Corp. and its owner for submitting claims for inflated or improperly prorated mileage under HCPCS Code P9603, travel allowance when only a fingerstick blood draw was performed, and travel allowance and laboratory services that were never rendered.

title: Greenwood Center for Nursing and Rehabilitation Agreed to Pay $83,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Greenwood submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed certified nursing assistant.

title: United States Intervenes and Sues ProMedica Health System, Inc. and Its Affiliates for Providing Grossly Substandard Nursing Home Services
scheme: The United States alleged that four nursing homes owned by ProMedica provided non-existent or grossly substandard skilled nursing facility care, failed to develop or follow individualized care plans, and falsely documented in resident medical records that care had been provided when it had not.

title: United States Intervenes and Sues ProMedica Health System, Inc. and Its Affiliates for Providing Grossly Substandard Nursing Home Services
scheme: The United States alleged that four nursing homes owned and controlled by ProMedica provided non-existent or grossly substandard skilled nursing facility care from 2017 to 2023, failed to develop or follow individualized care plans, and in some cases falsely documented in resident medical records that care had been provided when it had not.

title: Middletown Resident Charged in Health Care Fraud Scheme Involving Durable Medical Equipment
scheme: Habib and Around the World Solutions LLC billed Medicare Advantage plan sponsors for orthotics purportedly provided to more than 400 Medicare beneficiaries who did not request or receive them, and transferred proceeds to financial institutions in Pakistan.

title: Blood Test Lab Owner Pleads Guilty to Evading Over $11.2 Million in Federal Taxes by Using Shill to Illegally Collect Medicare Payments
scheme: Muradyan used a long-time friend as a shill owner to enroll his blood-testing laboratory with Medicare and collect reimbursements after Medicare banned him from submitting claims, evaded more than $11.2 million in federal taxes, and obtained $99,900 through a false EIDL application.

title: Owner of California Blood Testing Laboratory Pleads Guilty to Tax and Health Care Related Crimes
scheme: Muradyan owned and operated a blood testing laboratory that received more than $23 million in Medicare reimbursements while using a nominee owner and bank accounts, failed to report the income on tax returns, and submitted a false COVID-19 EIDL application.

title: Attorney General Ra˙l Torrez Charges Imposter Nurse Who Nearly Caused Fatal Dose of Morphine
