scheme: Hernandez, a certified nurse assistant, allegedly assumed the identities of two registered nurses and a licensed practical nurse to gain employment as a nurse and illegally provide care to hospice patients, receiving approximately $40,000 in compensation based on the fraudulent licenses and mis-transcribing a medication order that nearly led to a fatal dose of morphine.

title: Home health agency owner sentenced to more than six years in Medicare fraud and identity theft scheme
scheme: The owner of a home health agency forged signatures of doctors and nurses on doctors' orders, nursing notes and assessments and submitted the falsified records to Medicare to support claims, and bribed a doctor to approve home health services.

title: Danville Woman Sentenced for Health Care Fraud
scheme: Farrish submitted and approved fraudulent timesheets claiming 9,819 hours of personal care attendant services from her estranged husband that were never performed, causing a loss to Virginia Medicaid of $116,536.

title: AG Campbell Secures $12.25 Million Settlement With CVS For Failure To Comply With MassHealth Prescription Drug Pricing Regulations
scheme: CVS charged MassHealth, the state's Medicaid program, higher prices than it offered to the general public for the same drugs.

title: Louisville Physician Agrees to Pay $250,000 to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: The United States alleged that Dr. Charasika and LPCMH billed government programs as if he provided medical services when the services were provided by nurse practitioners, without satisfying the conditions for such billing.

title: Maryland Woman Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Commit Healthcare Fraud
scheme: The defendants conspired to submit false claims to Medicaid for nursing services that were not provided or were in excess of services provided, including paying parents or guardians of patients for blank, signed nursing notes and falsifying records to support the claims.

title: Ideal Health Diagnostics and Svetlana Dizik Agreed to Pay $227,000 and Be Excluded for 10 Years for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Improper Remuneration and Causing the Submission of False or Fraudulent Medicare Claims
scheme: Ideal Health solicited and received improper remuneration from Perry Rudich, MD in exchange for referrals for radiological interpretive services, and Ideal Health and Dizik caused the submission of Medicare claims that falsely identified Dr. Rudich as the rendering provider for items and services he did not perform and that they, as non-enrolled providers, could not bill.

title: Attorney General James Secures $12 Million and Major Reforms at Syracuse Nursing Home to Stop Resident Neglect and Financial Fraud
scheme: The owners of Van Duyn Center for Rehabilitation and Nursing took millions of dollars of Medicare and Medicaid funds meant for resident care through fraudulently inflated rental payments and salaries for work they did not perform, leaving the nursing home understaffed and residents neglected.

title: Waccamaw Dermatology Agreed to Pay $160,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims that Did Not Meet Medicare Requirements for Locum Tenens Coverage
scheme: Waccamaw Dermatology submitted claims for dermatopathology services provided by a physician under the National Provider Identification number of another physician with the Q6 modifier for locum tenens coverage, when the claims did not meet Medicare requirements for locum tenens coverage.

title: Compliance Director and Office Manager of Substance Abuse Company Convicted in Scheme to Pay Medicaid Kickbacks to Patients
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - North Carolina, Eastern
scheme: Two former leaders of a substance abuse treatment company used Medicaid reimbursement funds to buy more than $1 million in gift cards that were given weekly to patients to incentivize them to show up for services, made false statements and documents to Medicaid auditors, and received unreported kickbacks from a drug testing lab company.

title: North Central Ohio Family Care Center and Dr. James Heddleson Agreed to Pay $66,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims that Did Not Meet Billing Requirements
scheme: The Center received payments for services billed by Dr. James Heddleson for discharge day evaluation and management billed as performed at times after the patients were discharged.

title: Danville Woman Sentenced for Health Care Fraud
scheme: A Danville woman claimed to receive almost 10,000 hours of personal care services from her estranged husband that were never actually provided, causing a loss to Medicaid of over $116,000.

title: MISSISSIPPI MEDICAID RECIPIENTS AGREE TO PAY OVER $170,000 TO RESOLVE FALSE CLAIMS ACT ALLEGATIONS OF HEALTH CARE BENEFITS FRAUD
district: Department of Justice, USAO - Mississippi, Southern
scheme: Former Medicaid recipients allegedly falsified their income on Mississippi Medicaid applications and renewals to create eligibility for health care benefits for their dependents.

title: Crawford Drug Agreed to Pay $78,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Prescription Drugs Not Dispensed
scheme: OIG alleged that Crawford Drug submitted claims for prescription drugs but did not dispense the prescription drugs to patients.

title: The Grand Rehabilitation and Nursing at Utica Agreed to Pay $315,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: The Grand employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: BROOKLYN CARDIOLOGIST SENTENCED TO 37 MONTHS IN PRISON IN CONNECTION WITH HEALTH CARE FRAUD AND BRIBERY SCHEME
scheme: Mittal paid other providers purported rent payments to induce patient referrals to his Brooklyn clinic and fabricated patient records to bill for medically unnecessary peripheral vascular interventional procedures.

title: THREE BATON ROUGE INDIVIDUALS SENTENCED TO FEDERAL PRISON IN CONNECTION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE’S 2024 NATIONAL HEALTH CARE FRAUD ENFORCEMENT ACTION
scheme: Three individuals caused the submission of fraudulent prescriptions for controlled substances to Medicaid using the DEA registration numbers and identifying information of physicians and other medical providers without authority, and submitted false applications for federal pandemic assistance funds.

title: Illinois Doctor Sentenced to 34 Months in Prison for Evading $1.6M in Taxes and Committing Health Care Fraud
scheme: A doctor submitted false Medicare billings for in-home physician care episodes that did not occur, including for beneficiaries who were deceased or residing in inpatient facilities, while also evading payment of approximately $1.6 million in taxes.

title: Troy Health, Inc. Enters Non-Prosecution Agreement and Admits to Fraudulently Enrolling Medicare Beneficiaries and Identity Theft
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, USAO - North Carolina, Western
scheme: Troy admitted that from approximately October 2020 through the end of 2022 it unlawfully accessed pharmacy records and customer lists to obtain Medicare beneficiary information, made false statements on unsolicited sales calls, offered pharmacies kickbacks for enrollment referrals through its Troy.ai platform, and enrolled beneficiaries in its Medicare Advantage plans without their knowledge or consent.

title: Lackawanna man sentenced for defrauding Medicaid
scheme: Fadhel, an owner of a transportation company providing rides to Medicaid beneficiaries, submitted claims for shared rides which he certified as individual rides in order to claim a higher reimbursement amount.

title: California Behavioral Medicine Provider Agrees To Pay $2.75 Million To Resolve Alleged False Claims For Psychotherapy Services
scheme: CPS submitted false claims to government healthcare payors using psychotherapy add-on Current Procedural Terminology codes 90833 and 90836 without the required documentation for services performed in conjunction with an evaluation and management visit.

title: North Carolina Baptist Hospital Agreed to Pay $200,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Provide Appropriate Medical Screening Examinations
scheme: OIG concluded that on two occasions in August 2021, North Carolina Baptist Hospital failed to provide adequate medical screening examinations for two patients who presented to its Emergency Department, in violation of EMTALA.

title: Emerald Care Center Claremore Agreed to Pay $116,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Emerald submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed registered nurse.

title: Alabama Doctor Charged with $6 Million Telemedicine Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: An Alabama doctor worked with telemedicine companies to sign pre-populated orders for medically unnecessary durable medical equipment and genetic testing for Medicare beneficiaries he never contacted, resulting in over $6 million in claims submitted to Medicare.

title: Three Indicted in Multi-State Prescription Fraud Ring
scheme: Three defendants were arrested on an indictment charging healthcare fraud, healthcare fraud conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft in a prescription fraud ring that targeted pharmacies throughout the northeastern United States.

title: Saginaw Physician Charged with Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Carthron is alleged to have billed the Medicaid program for services never provided 23 times between May 31 and September 27, 2024, billed as telephone visits.

title: Oklahoma City Woman Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud
scheme: Allmon, a behavioral health counselor with an agreement with Blue Cross Blue Shield, submitted or caused to be submitted thousands of false claims for behavioral health counseling sessions for family members, including claims for treating beneficiaries more than 24 hours in a single day.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces Two Convictions and One Arrest by Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
scheme: McCullum billed Medicaid for personal-care services that she never provided to her clients, Hoyle used a victim's debit card for unauthorized purchases while employed as a caregiver, and Pelto was arrested for stealing money and property from a person for whom he served as co-guardian.

title: 10 Medicaid Providers Facing Fraud, Theft Charges
scheme: Nine home-health aides and one provider of home-delivered meals were indicted for allegedly billing Medicaid for services they did not provide, totaling a combined $1.9 million.

title: Bristol Regional Medical Center Agreed to Pay $150,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Provide Appropriate Medical Screening Examinations
scheme: OIG alleged that Bristol Regional Medical Center failed to provide an adequate medical screening examination for two patients who presented to its emergency department in May 2021 and July 2021, in violation of EMTALA.

title: AG Murrill's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit Arrests Slidell Woman For Cruel Attack On An Individual With A Disability Under Her Care
scheme: Ussin was charged with intentional mistreatment of an infirmed person under her care as the victim's direct service worker and through her company, after video showed her repeatedly striking a non-verbal intellectually disabled Louisiana Medicaid recipient with her hand, foot, and a fence gate.

title: Baltimore County Woman Admits to Impersonating Nurses, Pleads Guilty to Aggravated Identity Theft
scheme: Amponsah used stolen nursing licenses and false educational and professional histories to obtain employment as a purported licensed nurse at no less than 40 facilities in Maryland, which billed health care benefit programs including Medicare and Medicaid for services she provided.

title: AG's Office Secures Guilty Plea and Restitution from Worcester-Based Home Health Company and Administrator for MassHealth Fraud
scheme: A group adult foster care provider and its administrator pleaded guilty to charges related to a scheme to defraud MassHealth of more than $1.6 million.

title: Attorney General Raúl Torrez Files Lawsuit Alleging Over $1.6 Million in Fraudulent Medicaid Claims and Identity Theft of Children
scheme: The complaint alleges two operators of a nonprofit afterschool program submitted at least $1,626,496 in fraudulent Medicaid claims for services never rendered while using adult and children's social security numbers and Medicaid identifier numbers without consent and documenting false psychological disorders.

title: Swedish American Hospital Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Provide an Appropriate Medical Screening Examination and Stabilizing Treatment
scheme: OIG alleged that in 2024 the hospital failed to provide an appropriate medical screening examination and stabilizing treatment to a patient who presented to its Emergency Department with suicidal ideation and a petition for involuntary admission, and discharged the patient about two hours after presentment.

title: Conviction of Fawn Gobis for Theft and Medicaid Fraud
scheme: A Merrimack County jury found Fawn Gobis guilty of one felony count of Theft by Deception and two felony counts of Medicaid Fraud.

title: Four Men to Including Two Doctors to Charged in a $7 Million Illegal Opioid Distribution Conspiracy
scheme: The indictment alleges the defendants conspired to issue thousands of opioid prescriptions for supposed patients who did not have a legitimate medical need, resulting in more than 400,000 dosage units of Schedule II opioids with a street value over $7 million and more than $1 million fraudulently billed to Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary medications.

title: Connecticut Lab, its Owners and Officers, to Pay More Than $1.2 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Genco Lab and its owners and officers submitted claims to Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary urine drug tests performed for residential monitoring of sober home residents and for duplicative presumptive and definitive testing on the same day.

title: Legacy Health Agreed to Pay $709,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Sleep Study Services Not Provided and Paying Remuneration in the Form of Compensation for Services Not Provided
scheme: Legacy billed outpatient sleep study services by a physician that were not provided and paid remuneration to that physician in the form of compensation for services the physician did not provide.

title: Connecticut Lab and Owners to Pay More Than $1.2 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Genco Lab and its owners and officers submitted claims to Medicare and Connecticut Medicaid for medically unnecessary urine drug tests, including tests for residential monitoring of sober home residents and duplicative simultaneous screening and confirmation testing.

title: Superseding Indictment Against Pittsburgh Health Care Facility Owner Adds Charges of Social Security Fraud and Concealing Material Facts Related to Health Care Matters
scheme: As owner of SerenityCare LLC, Oliver-Hollis schemed to overbill Pennsylvania Medicaid in connection with services provided to residents with intellectual disabilities, and misused Social Security benefits as a representative payee.

title: Watonga Psychiatrist To Pay More Than $170,000 For False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: As operator of Richard Zielinski MD, PLLC, Zielinski allegedly upcoded claims for evaluating and managing patients and submitted them to SoonerCare for payment between Jan. 1, 2019, and June 30, 2021, and caused his agents and employees to fabricate records supporting the false claims after being notified of an audit.

title: Abdifatah Yusuf Found Guilty Of Bilking Medicaid Program Out Of Over $7.2 Million
scheme: Yusuf, through his agency Promise Health Services, LLC, which operated out of a mailbox, billed Medicaid for home and community based services that were not provided, based on false documentation, overbilled, or undocumented, and provided kickbacks to recipients to induce them to receive services.

title: United States Obtains More Than $1.4 Million Judgment Against Family Medical Practitioner for Fraudulent Billing
scheme: Akoto billed Medicare for auricular stimulation (P-Stim) devices using a code for a surgically implanted neurostimulator device, which Medicare does not reimburse as acupuncture.

title: Richmond psychotherapist convicted of healthcare fraud to pay over $1M
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: A licensed clinical social worker submitted at least $335,824.31 in fraudulent claims to Virginia Medicaid and Medicare for services that were not rendered, including billing for more than 16 hours of services in one day and using billing codes for more complex services than provided, supported by false psychotherapy progress notes.

title: Houston doctor agrees to pay over $2 million to settle allegations of fraudulent billing of federal programs
scheme: Aggarwal billed federally funded health care programs for surgical implantation of neurostimulator electrodes when patients instead received electro-acupuncture devices taped behind the ear in his clinic with no incision.

title: Allentown-Area Pharmacy and Its Owner Agree to Pay $825,000 to Resolve Allegations of False Claims Act Liability
scheme: A pharmacy and its owner-pharmacist billed Medicare for prescription medications that were not actually dispensed to Medicare beneficiaries between January 1, 2014, and February 24, 2019.

title: CEO of Spine Device Company Sentenced for False Statements in Connection With Mandatory Reporting to CMS
scheme: Chin directed employees to report a $4,750 payment to a surgeon to CMS as a consulting fee even though he knew the surgeon had not performed actual consulting work.

title: Illinois Man Charged in Durable Medical Equipment Scheme
scheme: Bhatia allegedly worked with co-conspirators to own and operate DME companies that paid telemarketing companies for orthotic brace orders and billed Medicare over $2 million for equipment that was medically unnecessary, unwanted by beneficiaries and tainted by kickbacks, and opened a new DME company after a payment suspension.

title: Jorden Borders sentenced to 468 months in prison
scheme: Borders was found guilty of three counts of child torture, three counts of stalking, four counts of theft by false representation, and one count of attempted murder involving her three children, in a case tried by the Attorney General's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and Criminal Division.

title: Elite Medical Transport Agreed to Pay $144,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Containing Forged and Invalid Signatures
scheme: OIG alleged that Elite submitted claims for ambulance transport services containing forged and otherwise invalid signatures.

title: Brooklyn Woman Pleads Guilty to Leading a $68 Million Social Adult Day Care and Home Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Khan owned two Brooklyn social adult day care centers and, with marketers she employed, paid kickbacks and bribes to Medicaid recipients for social adult day care services that were billed to Medicaid but not provided or were induced by kickbacks, and used multiple business entities to launder the proceeds.

title: University Physicians of Brooklyn Agreed to Pay $455,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Incident-to Services Not Covered
scheme: UPB submitted claims for services provided by nurse practitioners in the office setting billed as incident-to the services of physicians employed by UPB, although the nurse practitioners were not employed by or under contract with UPB.

title: Justice Department Files Two Civil Forfeiture Actions to Recover Nearly $11 Million in Health Care Fraud Proceeds
scheme: Two enrolled Medicare durable medical equipment companies submitted false and fraudulent claims for DME that was medically unnecessary and not provided as represented, and the United States filed civil forfeiture complaints to recover the proceeds.

title: Attorney General Tong Announces APRN and Medical Practice to Pay Over $600k And Cease Connecticut Medicaid Participation to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Ntchana and Integrated Procare Services billed Medicare and Connecticut Medicaid for services not rendered, services of an unlicensed provider, and upcoded or duplicative claims from January 2016 through October 2020.

title: Woodland Springs Agreed to Pay $188,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by Unlicensed Individuals
scheme: Woodland Springs submitted claims that included counseling services and psychological assessments provided by two unlicensed individuals.

title: APRN and Medical Practice to Pay Over $600k and Cease Connecticut Medicaid Participation to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Ntchana and his entities improperly billed Medicare and Connecticut Medicaid for services not rendered, the services of an unlicensed provider, and upcoded or duplicative claims.

title: Leader of $68M Adult Day Care Fraud Scheme Pleads Guilty
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, USAO - New York, Eastern
scheme: Khan and marketers she employed paid kickbacks and bribes to Medicaid recipients to refer them to her two Brooklyn social adult day cares, which billed Medicaid over $68 million for services that were not provided or were induced by kickbacks, and used multiple business entities to launder the proceeds.

title: Canton Man Pleads Guilty to Multi-Million-Dollar Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Gidwani and co-conspirators owned and operated a DME company that paid telemarketing companies for orthotic brace orders and submitted over $4 million in Medicare claims for equipment that was medically unnecessary, not wanted by beneficiaries and tainted by kickbacks.

title: Glendale Woman Sentenced to 9 Years in Federal Prison for $10.6 Million Hospice Fraud Scheme Involving Kickbacks for Patients
scheme: Palma, while excluded from Medicare, concealed her ownership of two hospices, paid marketers including Abrams kickbacks for patient referrals, and caused submission of approximately $10.6 million in fraudulent Medicare claims for purported hospice care for patients who were not dying.

title: AG's Office Secures Indictments Against Northampton Resident for Causing More Than $99,000 in False Claims to MassHealth
scheme: Boston submitted false timesheets to MassHealth for personal care attendant services that were never provided, resulting in MassHealth paying more than $99,000.

title: Zavier Ash, MD Agreed to Pay $209,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in Exchange for Prescribing Medications
scheme: Dr. Ash solicited and received remuneration, in the form of monetary payments related to purported telemedicine consultations, from telemedicine and staffing companies in exchange for ordering and prescribing medically unnecessary topical pain cream medications for Medicare beneficiaries he never examined.

title: St. Luke's Hospital of Duluth Agreed to Pay $214,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Remuneration in the Form of Free Technology Services
scheme: OIG alleged that St. Luke's paid remuneration to a referring orthopedic physician practice in the form of free information technology services and without a written agreement in place for the information technology services.

title: AG Campbell Secures $6 Million Settlement With Weymouth-Based Ambulance Companies For MassHealth False Claims
scheme: The companies and their owners submitted false claims to MassHealth for more expensive services than were provided, violated MassHealth medical necessity requirements, and failed to disclose relevant information in their MassHealth provider applications.

title: CEO and Medical Director Charged in $500M COVID-19 Test Billing Fraud
scheme: Fast Lab Technologies operated a website offering free COVID-19 tests, collected beneficiaries' insurance information, and billed Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and private insurers more than $500 million for antigen and PCR testing services that were never rendered.

title: The Pointe Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Agreed to Pay $74,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: The Pointe employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Greensboro Woman Sentenced in Conviction with Multi-Million Dollar Urine Drug Testing Scheme
scheme: A Greensboro woman was sentenced in connection with a scheme to submit claims for fraudulent urine drug testing screens to Medicaid.

title: Florida Woman to Pay $400,000 to Settle Allegations of Falsifying Diagnoses in connection with an Amherst Compounding Pharmacy
scheme: Exposito and her company allegedly violated the False Claims Act by submitting false claims to Medicare and TRICARE based on fake medical diagnoses in connection with an Amherst compounding pharmacy.

title: Broken Arrow Dentist To Pay More Than $500,000 After False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Cullens, as operator of Stonewood Hills Oral Maxillofacial Surgery Inc., allegedly submitted false claims to SoonerCare by double billing and upcoding patient encounters, billing excess units of general anesthesia and billing for tobacco cessation counseling for non-tobacco users.

title: Kidspeace National Centers of New England Agreed to Pay $44,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Contracting with an Excluded Individual
scheme: Kidspeace, through a contractor, employed an individual excluded from participating in any Federal health care program, a speech pathologist who provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Windsor Laurelwood Center for Behavioral Medicine Agreed to Pay $104,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Windsor Laurelwood employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: AG Sunday’s Medicaid Fraud Control Section Charges Philadelphia Pharmacy in $2 Million Scheme Involving Sales of Unregulated HIV Medication
scheme: A pharmacy dispensed unregulated HIV medications not obtained from authorized wholesale distributors and claimed more than $2 million in Medicaid and Medicare reimbursements as if the drugs came from legitimate distributors.

title: Dermatology Providers Agree to Pay Nearly $850,000 to Resolve Allegations of False Wound Repair Claims
scheme: The providers agreed to pay $847,394 to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by knowingly causing the submission of falsely coded claims to Medicare for wound repair procedures.

title: Urology Group of Florida Agreed to Pay $25,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Urology Group of Florida employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: NHC Healthcare to Burlington Agreed to Pay $31,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that NHC Burlington submitted claims to Federal health care programs for services provided by an unlicensed practical nurse.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces Arrest of Trumann Man for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Vales was listed as an employee and caregiver at First Choice Home Care despite never providing any legitimate services, and using his fraudulent profile submitted claims to Medicaid for services that were never rendered between June 13, 2022, and December 26, 2023, resulting in $96,711.68 in fraudulent payments.

title: AG’s Office Secures Guilty Plea, Restitution From New Bedford Clinical Lab For MassHealth Fraud And Kickback Schemes
scheme: Optimum Labs and its owner submitted false claims for sober home urine drug tests that were not payable by MassHealth, including tests that were medically unnecessary, not performed or properly authorized, and/or resulted from illegal kickback arrangements.

title: Florida Man Sentenced To More Than 17 Years For Scheme To Steal More Than $10.8 Million From Medicare
scheme: Gutierrez and co-conspirators created sham DME companies that submitted over $10.8 million in fraudulent Medicare claims for braces that beneficiaries did not want or need, procured through kickbacks paid for signed doctors' orders obtained via overseas call centers and telemedicine companies.

title: Louisiana Nurse Practitioner Convicted of $12M Medicare Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Louisiana, Eastern
scheme: A nurse practitioner signed hundreds of orders for medically unnecessary cancer genetic tests for patients she never met or examined, in exchange for kickbacks from a telehealth company, causing over $12.1 million in fraudulent Medicare claims.

title: Attorney General Jeff Jackson Secures Over $200 Million from Gilead Sciences for Paying Kickbacks to Doctors
scheme: Gilead Sciences paid kickbacks to doctors in exchange for promoting its HIV medications, resulting in false claims submitted to government health care programs including North Carolina's Medicaid program.

title: United States Reaches $501,556 Civil Settlement Resolving Allegations of False Claims to Federal Health Care Programs
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Missouri, Eastern
scheme: From Jan. 1, 2019, through May 31, 2024, a psychiatrist falsely indicated to Medicare and Missouri Medicaid that he provided face-to-face psychotherapy to patients, including submitting claims for payment when he was out of town and for services provided by other practitioners.

title: Eye Consultants of Pennsylvania, PC Agrees To Pay $790,000.00 To Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Eye Consultants of Pennsylvania, PC submitted claims to Medicare for Evaluation & Management services that violated Medicare rules and regulations.

title: Woodlands Senior Living of Cape Elizabeth Agreed to Pay $270,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Woodlands employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Attorney General Ken Paxton's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit Plays Key Role in Largest Dismantling of Health Care Fraud in U.S. History. U.S.
scheme: Texas Medicaid Fraud Control Unit participated in a national enforcement action resulting in criminal charges against 30 defendants in more than a dozen health care fraud schemes in Texas involving more than $177 million in fraudulent bills, $1.7 million in bribes, and diversion of more than 10 million opioid pills.

title: New Jersey Doctor Charged With Distributing Opioids In Exchange For Sexual Favors And Defrauding New Jersey Medicaid
scheme: A physician was charged with distributing opioids outside the usual course of professional practice in exchange for sexual favors and billing New Jersey Medicaid for in-person visits and counseling sessions that never occurred.

title: City of Fort Dodge Agreed to Pay $32,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that the City of Fort Dodge submitted claims to Federal health care programs for services provided by an unlicensed paramedic.

title: Medfleet Agreed to Pay $81,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Improperly Licensed Emergency Medical Responder
scheme: Medfleet submitted claims to Federal health care programs for services provided by an improperly licensed emergency medical responder.

title: Rossi Sentenced to an Additional Three Years in Prison for Healthcare Fraud Related to COVID Testing
district: Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Illinois, Central
scheme: Rossi, through his laboratory Reditus Labs, submitted claims with codes for COVID testing services that were never performed and received payments from more than one source for the same test.

title: Physician Assistant who Pretended to be a Licensed Physician Pleads Guilty to Making False Statements to an Agency of the United States
district: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Puerto Rico
scheme: Villalobos-Meléndez, a licensed physician assistant who was never licensed to practice medicine, forged medical license and USMLE documents, worked as a physician in a hospital internship program, and submitted false license information on a CMS-855I form seeking enrollment as a Medicare physician provider with benefits reassigned to Physician HMO.

title: United States and the States of Georgia, Colorado, and South Carolina Obtain $114.5M in Judgments in a Sprawling Cancer Genetic Testing Lab Scheme
scheme: Premier Medical, its owner and compliance vice president paid kickbacks to Freedom Medical Labs and its marketers, who collected DNA samples from Medicaid beneficiaries in public spaces and purchased telemedicine physician orders, to bill Medicaid for medically unnecessary cancer genetic testing.

title: Florida Man Admits Role in $4.8 Million Health Care Fraud and Kickback Scheme
scheme: Kasbee and co-conspirators used marketing call centers to obtain Medicare beneficiaries' information, arranged for cancer genetic screening test kits to be sent and shipped to a testing laboratory that billed Medicare, and received kickbacks exceeding $1,200 per reimbursed test disguised as expenses on false invoices.

title: AG Jennings Secures over $96K Settlement Following HIV Drug Kickback Investigation
scheme: Delaware joined other states and the federal government in an agreement in principle with an unnamed HIV drug manufacturer, following a kickback investigation, that will return $96,571.13 to Delaware's Medicaid program.

title: AG Campbell Announces Over $1 Million Settlement With Worcester County Transportation Provider For Defrauding MassHealth And Department Of Developmental Services
scheme: The company submitted false claims to MassHealth and the Department of Developmental Services for contracted routes not actually driven and failed to have required staff monitors onboard for certain routes.

title: Attorney General Dan Rayfield Helps Secure $202 Million Settlement with Gilead Over Kickback Scheme Involving HIV Medications
scheme: Gilead paid honoraria, expensive meals, and travel perks to doctors who attended or spoke at promotional events for its HIV drugs from 2011 to 2017, leading to false claims submitted to government health care programs.

title: Nevada Nurse Practitioner Pleads Guilty To Fraudulent Medicare Wound Care Billing
scheme: A nurse practitioner admitted conspiring to fraudulently bill Medicare approximately $14,333,550 for amniotic wound allografts that were medically unnecessary and were procured through illegal kickbacks and bribes.

title: Attorney General Raoul Announces More Than $200 Million Settlement With Gilead Sciences Over Illegal Kickbacks To Providers For Prescriptions
scheme: From January 2011 to November 2017, Gilead provided gifts, speaker program payments, travel expenses and meals to health care providers to induce prescriptions of its HIV medications, resulting in false claims to government health care programs.

title: New York Man Admits Health Care Fraud Scheme for Submitting Falsified Prescriptions to Medicare and Medicaid
scheme: Conzo submitted hundreds of thousands of dollars of fraudulent claims for prescriptions to Medicare and Medicaid on behalf of Elite Pharmacy using the credentials of pharmacists who did not work at the pharmacy or authorize the prescriptions.

title: AG Sunday Part of National Coalition Securing $200M+ from Gilead Sciences for Illegal Kickback Scheme to Sell HIV Drugs
scheme: From January 2011 to November 2017, Gilead violated federal anti-kickback laws by providing gifts, awards, meals, and travel expenses to health care providers who attended and spoke at promotional speaker programs for its HIV drugs, resulting in false claims submitted to government health care programs.

title: Frankfort Regional Medical Center Agreed to Pay $110,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Provide an Appropriate Medical Screening Examination
scheme: OIG alleged that Frankfort Regional Medical Center failed to provide an appropriate medical screening examination to a patient who presented to its emergency department with heat exhaustion and discharged him to jail with a clinical note of drug overdose.

title: AG Campbell Secures $1.6 Million For Massachusetts In Multi-State Settlement With Pharmaceutical Company
scheme: Gilead Sciences allegedly paid kickbacks to providers to improperly promote its HIV drugs, resolved in a multi-state settlement.

title: Attorney General Formella Helps Secure Over $200 Million from Gilead Sciences for Illegal Kickbacks
scheme: Gilead Sciences, Inc. ran an illegal kickback scheme to promote its HIV medications.

title: Attorney General James Secures Over $200 Million from Gilead Sciences for Paying Illegal Kickbacks
scheme: From January 2011 to November 2017, Gilead provided incentives including awards, meals, and travel expenses to health care providers to induce prescriptions of its HIV medications, resulting in false claims to government health care programs.

title: Healthcare Worker Pleads Guilty to Double Billing District of Columbia Medicaid Programs
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Office of the Inspector General, USAO - District of Columbia
scheme: Chapajong submitted false timesheets to his employers claiming to have provided in-person personal care aide services and telephonic behavioral health services to multiple District Medicaid beneficiaries simultaneously while at different locations, causing the District's Medicaid program to pay $113,243 for services he did not render.

title: Urgent Care Operator Pays $3 Million to Resolve Alleged Violations of the False Claims Act
scheme: Bloom Care LLC and its owners paid $3,000,000 to resolve allegations that they submitted false claims to Federal healthcare programs for medically unnecessary testing and for inflating the extent of services performed at urgent care centers in Idaho and New Mexico during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Law Enforcement Recovers Over $6 Million in Forfeited Assets from Miami Couple Sentenced to 9- and 3-Year Prison Terms for Health Care Fraud and Money Laundering Conspiracies
scheme: Travieso, owner of ProMed Healthcare, conspired with others to submit over $20 million in fraudulent claims by paying patients kickbacks and fabricating medical records for medically unnecessary or never-provided goods and services, and Ramirez laundered the proceeds.

title: California Man Pleads Guilty in Connection with $16M Hospice Fraud Scheme and Money Laundering Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - California, Central
scheme: Esparza and co-defendants operated four sham hospice companies that billed Medicare nearly $16 million for hospice services that were not medically necessary and never provided, using foreign nationals' identifying information, and laundered the proceeds through shell company accounts.

title: SPARC Network Agreed to Pay $181,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that SPARC employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Corvallis Clinic Agreed to Pay $108,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying and Receiving Remuneration in the Form of Referrals and Receiving Remuneration in the Form of Referral Fees
scheme: OIG alleged that Corvallis Clinic paid remuneration to an ophthalmologist and his practice in the form of routine referrals of Medicare patients requiring intraocular lens implant surgery and received remuneration from the ophthalmologist and his practice in the form of per patient referral fees and routine referrals of IOL surgery patients back to Corvallis Clinic for post-operative services billed with modifier-55.

title: Home Health Care Provider To Pay $334,807 To Settle False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: M&Y Care billed Medicare and Medicaid under CPT code G0156 for home health aide services provided by staff who lacked the requisite qualifications and were insufficiently trained, when it should have billed for non-skilled care.

title: UAB Medical West Agreed to Pay $100,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statue by Failing to Provide Stabilizing Treatment
scheme: OIG concluded that UAB Medical West failed to provide stabilizing treatment to a patient diagnosed with acute urinary retention at its freestanding emergency department and discharged him with instructions to drive himself to another facility.

title: Andrew Gomes, MD Was Excluded for Defaulting on Payment Obligations
scheme: OIG excluded Andrew Gomes, MD for defaulting on his payment obligations under a False Claims Act Settlement Agreement entered into for paying improper remuneration to physicians for referrals to clinics established to surgically treat patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces Arrest of Paragould Woman for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Rios is accused of submitting claims and time sheets for services she did not provide, and some listed clients said she had never been their caregiver.

title: 9 Medicaid Providers Indicted on Fraud Charges
scheme: Nine Medicaid providers, eight home-health aides and one mental-health specialist, were indicted for allegedly billing Medicaid a combined $1.2 million for services they did not provide.

title: Ohio Doctor Pleads Guilty to Role in Telemedicine Scheme
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Ohio, Northern
scheme: Ahmad signed pre-completed orders authorizing orthotic braces and other durable medical equipment as medically necessary for Medicare beneficiaries he did not examine, causing approximately $267,402 in false and fraudulent claims to be submitted to Medicare.

title: Department of Justice Subpoenas Doctors and Clinics Involved in Performing Transgender Medical Procedures on Children
scheme: The Department of Justice sent more than 20 subpoenas to doctors and clinics involved in performing transgender medical procedures on children as part of investigations including healthcare fraud and false statements.

title: MUSC Physicians Agreed to Pay $225,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Psychotherapy that Were Not Provided as Claimed
scheme: OIG alleged that MUSC Physicians submitted claims for telehealth psychotherapy services for longer psychotherapy sessions than were provided.

title: St. Joseph Living Center Agreed to Pay $88,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that St. Joseph employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Brant Jolly Agreed to Be Excluded for 10 Years for Allegedly Submitting False Claims for Lab Tests
scheme: OIG alleged that Brant Jolly caused the submission of false claims to Medicare for lab tests that were never ordered, never rendered, and/or involved deceased beneficiaries.

title: 1st Choice Healthcare Agreed to Pay $31,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Chronic Care Management that Were Not Provided as Claimed
scheme: 1st Choice submitted false claims to Federal health care programs for more Chronic Care Management minutes than were actually provided by a CCM nurse employed by 1st Choice.

title: Shasta View Care Center Agreed to Pay $41,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Fraudulent Nursing Services
scheme: OIG alleged that Shasta View Care Center submitted claims for fraudulent nursing services.

title: Two California Residents Plead Guilty in Connection with $16M Hospice Fraud Scheme and Money Laundering Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - California, Central
scheme: Defendants used four sham hospice companies and misappropriated identities of foreign nationals and doctors to bill Medicare nearly $16 million for hospice services that were not medically necessary and never provided, and laundered the proceeds.

title: Former Chief Operating Officer of Pain Care Centers Sentenced
scheme: The former chief operating officer of L5 Medical Holdings, doing business as Pain Care Centers, helped conceal illegal prescribing and healthcare fraud at the clinics, including directing medical decisions by non-medical staff, using doctors' prescribing credentials for patients they had not seen, and implementing drug testing policies that inflated bills to medical insurers.

title: Attorney General Murrill secures over $200 million from Gilead Sciences for paying Illegal Kickbacks
scheme: From January 2011 to November 2017, Gilead provided gifts, awards, meals, and travel expenses to health care providers who attended and spoke at promotional speaker programs for its HIV drugs to induce prescriptions, resulting in false claims to government health care programs.

title: United States Files False Claim Act Complaint Against Delaware Medical Provider
scheme: The United States alleges that Dr. Mufti referred more than 100 Medicare beneficiaries for medically unnecessary genetic laboratory tests based on brief telemedicine consultations or no consultation, causing false claims to Medicare.

title: Former Delaware Nurse Practitioner Resolves Health Care Fraud Allegations
scheme: A former nurse practitioner digitally signed hundreds of orders for genetic testing and durable medical equipment for Medicare beneficiaries she never physically examined and with whom she had no pre-existing provider-patient relationship, resulting in Medicare paying approximately $520,000.

title: Adult Foster Home Owner Pleads Guilty to Neglect and Theft Charges Involving Medicaid Recipients
scheme: Woodring billed Medicaid several hundred thousand dollars for adult foster home services never properly provided while housing residents at an unlicensed location and withholding medical and physical care, resulting in one resident's death from untreated cancer.

title: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 87 Months in Prison and Administrator Sentenced to 72 Months for their Respective Roles in a Health Care Fraud and Kickback Scheme
scheme: The co-owner and administrator of a Union City, New Jersey specialty pharmacy conspired to bill Medicare, Medicaid, and private health benefit providers through PBMs for prescription refills that were never dispensed and to pay kickbacks to doctors and their staffs for prescription referrals.

title: Bonita Man Pleads Guilty in $5.8 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme
scheme: Melcer submitted more than $5.88 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare through two durable medical equipment companies selling orthotic braces, paid more than $227,000 in kickbacks for beneficiary referrals and prescriptions signed by physicians without a legitimate doctor-patient relationship, and sold the companies to a co-conspirator under a nominee owner to conceal ownership from Medicare.

title: Attorney General Nessel Announces $4.5 Million Settlement with Detroit Nursing Homes Over Substandard Care Allegations
scheme: Six Detroit-area nursing homes and their ownership companies allegedly accepted taxpayer funds while providing grossly substandard care to residents, including insufficient staffing, failure to prevent and treat infections, falls, and pressure ulcers, and failure to provide for toileting needs.

title: Tonawanda doctor pleads guilty for his role in prescription scam
scheme: A family practice doctor signed pre-filled compounded medication prescriptions for 19 individuals who were not his patients based on another person's representations of medical need, and later concealed this during a pharmacy benefit manager audit, resulting in $8,750,315 in reimbursements by health care benefit programs.

title: National Health Care Fraud Takedown Results in 324 Defendants Charged in Fraud Scheme Totaling Over $14.6 Billion
district: Criminal Division, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Louisiana, Eastern
scheme: Four defendants were charged in the Eastern District of Louisiana with schemes including billing Medicare for medically unnecessary genetic testing procured through kickbacks and purported telemedicine, billing Medicare for over-the-counter COVID-19 tests that were not requested, and embezzling federal grant funds from a non-profit.

title: Doctor Arrested For Multimillion-Dollar COVID-19 Insurance Scheme
scheme: Rashan, the founder and CEO of ClearMD, directed the submission of fraudulent claims to insurers for unperformed COVID-19 testing and evaluation and management services and had software generate false medical records to support the billings, resulting in losses of at least approximately $24 million.

title: Durable Medical Equipment Owner Sentenced to 12 Years for $61 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Roussonicolos secretly owned and operated five durable medical equipment suppliers using nominee owners and falsified enrollment and bank records to conceal his ineligibility, and the companies submitted approximately $61.5 million in false claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary DME, with kickbacks paid to patient recruiters for beneficiary referrals.

title: AG Sunday Charges PA. Therapist Accused Of Sexploiting Patient As Part Of the 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown
scheme: Pennsylvania charged a former counselor with billing Medical Assistance for therapy sessions during which he engaged in sexual acts with a patient, and a blended case manager with billing Medical Assistance for case management services he never provided to 54 clients.

title: The New England Strike Force Joins Nationwide Crackdown on Health Care Fraud
district: USAO - Maine, USAO - New Hampshire, USAO - Vermont
scheme: Six defendants were charged in New England in connection with unrelated schemes including billing NH Medicaid while excluded, submitting false Medicare claims for durable medical equipment such as wrist, knee, and back braces, money laundering, fulfilling illegitimate prescriptions for drugs including Ozempic, and using a stolen identity to obtain Medicaid and SNAP benefits, totaling over $14 million.

title: Four Individuals Charged in Northern District of Texas with Health Care Fraud Schemes Totaling over $210 Million as part of National Takedown
