title: Mountain View of Cascadia Agreed to Pay $33,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Mountain View submitted claims for medication administered by an individual who was not licensed to administer medication.

title: New York Man Convicted of Medicaid Fraud and Tax Evasion, Will Pay $1.8 Million in Restitution
scheme: Schwartz, principal owner and president of Skyline Healthcare, LLC, which operated Arkansas nursing homes receiving Medicaid payments, submitted false and misleading information that impacted the per diem rates paid to the facilities, and withheld employee taxes without remitting them to the state.

title: Emory Healthcare Network Agreed to Pay $1 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Remuneration to Physicians
scheme: OIG alleged that Emory paid remuneration to certain primary care physicians if the primary care physicians' Medicare Advantage and commercially insured patients received services from a specialist physician within Emory's network.

title: Wethersfield Woman Admits Role in Scheme that Defrauded Connecticut’s Medicaid Program of More Than $1.8 Million
scheme: Aponte, who is not a licensed provider, used Minds Cornerstone LLC with a co-conspirator to submit fraudulent claims to the Connecticut Medicaid Program for applied behavior analysis services to children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder.

title: Cumberland County Drug and Alcohol Rehabilitation Center Agrees to Pay $19.75 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Seabrook submitted claims to the VHA Community Care Program and New Jersey Medicaid for short-term residential treatment and partial hospitalization care for which it was not properly licensed or contracted, concealed unlicensed services from state inspectors, failed to employ sufficient properly credentialed caregivers, and kept false and inadequate records.

title: U.S. Attorney Announces $202 Million Settlement With Gilead Sciences For Using Speaker Programs To Pay Kickbacks To Doctors To Induce Them To Prescribe Gilead’s Drugs
scheme: Gilead offered and paid kickbacks in the form of honoraria payments, meals, and travel expenses to healthcare practitioners who spoke at or attended Gilead speaker events to induce them to prescribe Gilead HIV drugs, causing false claims to be submitted to federal healthcare programs.

title: Philadelphia Man Pleads Guilty to Defrauding the Government of More Than $1 Million in SNAP, Medicaid Benefits
scheme: Sessoms used stolen and fictitious identities and Social Security numbers, along with fraudulent identification and birth certificates, to file false applications for SNAP and Medicaid benefits and sold the fraudulently acquired SNAP cards, causing a total government loss of $1,063,633.

title: Jury Convicts Florida Man For Stealing $10.9 Million From Medicare
scheme: Gutierrez and co-conspirators owned and operated two durable medical equipment companies that billed Medicare more than $10.9 million for medically unnecessary braces obtained by paying kickbacks to marketing companies for signed doctors' orders, and concealed his role using straw owners.

title: Harlingen couple guilty in multimillion-dollar Medicare fraud scheme
scheme: The operators of a durable medical equipment company admitted receiving millions of dollars from Medicare for power wheelchair parts and repairs that were never performed or provided.

title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Announces Final Arrest In Massive Medicaid Fraud Case
scheme: Defendants operated a nonemergency medical transportation service that billed Medicaid for thousands of trips never provided and inflated mileage on actual trips.

title: Attorney General Griffin Announces Convictions Of Van Buren Father And Son For Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Ronald helped Garrett bill Medicaid for personal care services for Garrett's sibling that were never provided, and the two shared the proceeds of those billings.

title: Home Health Agency To Pay $100,000 In Settlement Over Incomplete Patient Care Records
scheme: Maxim Healthcare Services documented home health aide services in a manner found insufficient in an audit upheld by the state Administrative Appeals Unit and continued documenting services in the same manner.

title: Two former laboratory sales executives sentenced to federal prison for roles in health care kickback conspiracy
scheme: Laboratory sales executives conspired to violate the Anti-Kickback Statute by using management services organizations to disguise kickbacks to physicians as investment returns in exchange for laboratory test referrals to rural hospitals and an affiliated lab.

title: Massachusetts Doctor Agrees to Plead Guilty to $35.5 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme
scheme: A doctor signed or caused others to sign false medical documentation and orders for beneficiaries' genetic testing, falsely stating she had consulted with and examined beneficiaries, causing laboratories to submit approximately $35.3 million in claims to Medicare.

title: John H. Stroger, Jr. Hospital of Cook County Agreed to Pay $456,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing Individuals Excluded from Illinois Medicaid
scheme: OIG alleged that Stroger employed two individuals that it knew or should have known were excluded from participation in the Illinois state Medicaid program and that no Illinois state Medicaid program payments could be made for items or services the individuals furnished.

title: Former Owner Of York Pain Management Practice Sentenced To 42 Months For Health Care Fraud, Money Laundering, And Theft Of Public Money
scheme: Yentzer agreed with others to defraud Medicare by submitting medically unnecessary urine drug tests for chronic opioid patients at clinics he controlled, laundered the proceeds for personal benefit, and obtained over $191,000 in HHS COVID-19 provider relief funds after the clinics closed.

title: Former Director Of Tuscola County Peer Center Sentenced For Embezzling From Center
scheme: The former director of the Tuscola County Peer Center, which receives much of its funding from Medicaid, embezzled over $1,000 of the Center's funds for personal use.

title: Ex-Orange County Resident Sentenced to 7 Years in Federal Prison for Receiving Kickbacks from Sober Living Homes, Firearms Trafficking
scheme: Moore solicited and received nearly $500,000 in kickbacks from addiction treatment facilities for referring patients whose private health insurance plans the facilities billed for treatment services, and he also sold firearms while on pretrial release.

title: Maxim Healthcare Services Agreed to Pay $676,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Not Performed or that Did Not Meet Coverage Criteria
scheme: After self-disclosing conduct to OIG, Maxim submitted claims for services that were not performed or did not meet coverage criteria.

title: Vault Agrees to Pay $8 Million to Settle Allegations of Billing False Claims to the COVID-19 Uninsured Program for Patients with Health Insurance
scheme: Vault knowingly submitted or caused the submission of false claims to the HRSA COVID-19 Uninsured Program for COVID-19 testing and vaccine administration services provided to patients who had active health insurance.

title: Former Detroit Pharmacist Charged With Fraud
scheme: Onimo, owner of Divine Pharmacy, allegedly continued to fill prescriptions, including prescriptions billed to and paid by Medicaid, while his Michigan pharmacist license was suspended.

title: Genetic Testing Marketing Companies Genexe, LLC and Immerge, Inc. and Two Executives Agree to Pay $6 Million to Resolve Allegations of Fraudulent Medicare Claims
scheme: Genexe, Immerge, Green, and Gross allegedly participated in schemes that caused Medicare to pay claims for genetic testing that was medically unnecessary and procured through kickbacks, paying independent contractors to collect swabs from beneficiaries and paying providers for test orders while receiving a portion of laboratory Medicare reimbursements.

title: Kadlec Regional Medical Center Agreed to Pay $8.9 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services that Did Not Meet Coverage Criteria
scheme: OIG alleged that Kadlec submitted claims to Medicare Part A for inpatient hospital stays that did not meet coverage criteria under the two-midnight rule and claims to Medicare Part B for intravenous hydration administration for hospital outpatients in the emergency department that did not meet Medicare coverage criteria.

title: Memphis Woman Sentenced in Healthcare Fraud Scheme and Schemes to Defraud COVID-19 Relief Program
scheme: Cannady fraudulently billed Cigna Insurance for 24 hours a day of home healthcare when she knew the patients had only received 8 or 12 hours a day, and submitted six fraudulent PPP and EIDL applications containing false information for four businesses she controlled.

title: GreenField Health System Agreed to Pay $286,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Requesting Payment from Beneficiaries in Violation of an Assignment Agreement
scheme: OIG alleged that GreenField charged annual membership fees to Medicare beneficiaries in violation of an assignment agreement.

title: CHI St. Joseph Health - Saint Joseph Hospital Agreed to Pay $133,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Accept an Appropriate Transfer
scheme: OIG concluded that in February 2023 the hospital violated EMTALA when it failed to accept an appropriate transfer of a patient with bilateral pulmonary embolisms and an intra-abdominal abscess from another facility's emergency department that lacked the specialized capabilities to treat the patient.

title: Kyle Perkins Indicted for Conspiracy To Commit Medicaid Fraud
scheme: A grand jury indicted Kyle Perkins on charges of conspiracy to commit Medicaid fraud, identity fraud, and theft by deception.

title: Lawton-Area Trio Sentenced to Serve More Than 12 Years Collectively in Federal Prison for Health Care Fraud
scheme: The defendants conspired to submit false and fraudulent claims to TRICARE through two massage therapy businesses for services that were never rendered, including billing under the NPI of an occupational therapist who no longer worked there.

title: Walgreens Agrees To Pay Up to $350M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and Submitting False Claims
district: Office of the Attorney General, Civil Division, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), USAO - Illinois, Northern
scheme: Walgreens allegedly filled millions of invalid prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances in violation of the Controlled Substances Act and sought payment for many of those prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs in violation of the False Claims Act.

title: Walgreens Agrees to Pay Up to $350M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
district: Office of the Attorney General, Civil Division, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), USAO - Florida, Middle, USAO - Illinois, Northern, USAO - Maryland, USAO - New York, Eastern, USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: Walgreens allegedly filled millions of invalid controlled substance prescriptions, including excessive opioid quantities, early refills, and "trinity" combinations, and then sought payment for many of those prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Walgreens Agrees to Pay Up to $350 Million for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
scheme: Walgreens allegedly filled millions of unlawful controlled substance prescriptions, including excessive-quantity opioid prescriptions, early refills, and "trinity" combinations, and then sought payment for many of those invalid prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Walgreens Agrees to Pay Up to $350M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
district: Office of the Attorney General, Civil Division, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), USAO - Florida, Middle, USAO - Illinois, Northern, USAO - Maryland, USAO - New York, Eastern, USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: Walgreens allegedly knowingly filled millions of unlawful controlled substance prescriptions, including for excessive quantities of opioids, early refills, and "trinity" drug combinations, and sought payment for many of those invalid prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Operators of New Jersey Company Sentenced to Prison and Enter into Related Civil Settlement Agreement for Roles in $127 Million Health Care Fraud and Kickback Scheme
scheme: Two operators of a New Jersey marketing company paid and received kickbacks with telemedicine companies, doctors, and DME suppliers to generate medically unnecessary durable medical equipment orders, causing over $127 million in false claims to Medicare and TRICARE.

title: Walgreens agrees to pay up to $350M for illegally filling unlawful opioid prescriptions and for submitting false claims to the Federal Government
scheme: Walgreens allegedly filled millions of invalid prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances in violation of the Controlled Substances Act and then sought payment for many of those prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs in violation of the False Claims Act.

title: Walgreens Agrees to Pay Up to $350M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
scheme: Walgreens allegedly filled millions of invalid controlled substance prescriptions, including excessive opioid quantities, early refills, and "trinity" combinations, and then sought payment for many of those prescriptions from Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Executive Vice President of Insurance Brokerage Pleads Guilty in $133M Affordable Care Act Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Iza and accomplices submitted false and fraudulent applications that inflated consumers' incomes to enroll ineligible individuals in fully subsidized Affordable Care Act plans in order to obtain commission payments, with the federal government paying at least $133,900,000 in subsidies.

title: Connex Family Services Pays $1,600 Stipulated Penalty for Breaching Integrity Agreement
scheme: Connex Family Services paid a $1,600 stipulated penalty for failing to timely submit the first annual report required by its Integrity Agreement.

title: The Arthritis Knee Pain Centers and Dr. John Rush Face Federal Civil False Claims Allegations
scheme: The United States alleges that AKPC and Dr. Rush knowingly submitted or caused the submission of millions of dollars in false claims to Medicare for medically unreasonable and unnecessary knee injections performed on separate dates for each knee and for more contrast dye than they actually used.

title: Waterbury Man Arrested In Scheme To Defraud Medicaid
scheme: Marion billed Medicaid for personal care assistant and independent living skills services he did not provide while residing in Texas, and submitted timesheets for a co-conspirator who did not provide services and shared the payments with him.

title: Charles Nevels, MD Pays $74,000 Stipulated Penalty for Breaching Integrity Agreement
scheme: Charles T. Nevels, MD paid a $74,000 stipulated penalty for failing to submit the first annual report in accordance with the requirements of his Integrity Agreement.

title: Pharmacist indicted in $2 million health care fraud scheme
scheme: A pharmacist submitted or caused the submission of fraudulent claims to Medicaid for prescriptions that a doctor had never prescribed, using doctors' personal information without their consent.

title: Dayton Woman Gets Prison For $1.5 Million Theft From Medicaid Program
scheme: Corbitt stole multiple identities to open and operate two sham behavioral-health-counseling agencies in the Dayton area and used stolen credentials of licensed counselors to bill Medicaid for services that were never provided.

title: Baptist Health Medical Group Agreed to Pay $47,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: After self-disclosing to OIG, BHMG agreed to pay $47,553.54 for allegedly employing an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Physician Convicted at Trial for Illegal Distribution of Opioids and Healthcare Fraud Conspiracies
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Anand conspired to submit false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, OPM health plans, Independence Blue Cross, and Anthem for "Goody Bags" of medically unnecessary prescription medications dispensed by his in-house pharmacies, required patients to take them to receive controlled substance prescriptions, conspired to distribute oxycodone outside the usual course of professional practice using blank pre-signed prescriptions written by unlicensed medical interns, and transferred approximately $1.2 million of proceeds into an account in his father's name.

title: Former Nurse Practitioner Agrees to $50,000 Settlement in Alleged False Claims Act Violations
scheme: A former nurse practitioner digitally signed hundreds of orders for medically unnecessary orthotic braces for Medicare beneficiaries she never physically examined, following telemedicine consultations of often two minutes or less, on forms pre-populated by telemarketers.

title: Christopher Mallavarapu, MD Agreed to Pay $305,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in Exchange for Ordering Durable Medical Equipment, Genetic Testing, and Prescription Medications
scheme: Mallavarapu received remuneration in the form of monetary payments related to telemedicine and diagnostic consultations from telemedicine and staffing companies in exchange for ordering and prescribing durable medical equipment, genetic testing, and prescription medications for Medicare beneficiaries.

title: Panamanian Doctor Pleads Guilty in Criminal Fraud Case Expected to Save U.S. Government $25M
scheme: Panamanian doctors and pharmacies submitted false and inflated claims to the VA's Foreign Medical Program, including claims for services never rendered or medicines never received, as well as deceptive billing for services performed.

title: Florida Woman Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Defraud Medicare of $3.3 Million
scheme: Dupont served as nominee owner of Allstar Medical Supply Corp., a purported durable medical equipment business, and with co-conspirators submitted or caused the submission of approximately $3.3 million in false claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary orthotic braces.

title: Ashland City Doctor Sentenced to 3 Years for Conspiracy to Commit Health Care Fraud
district: Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Tennessee, Middle
scheme: Manning signed doctor orders and prescriptions for durable medical equipment, topical creams, and cancer genetic tests for telemedicine companies based on brief or no patient conversations in exchange for kickbacks and bribes, causing the submission of false and fraudulent claims to Medicare.

title: Union City Pharmacy Agrees To Resolve False Claims Act Allegations Of Billing For Drugs Not Dispensed
scheme: The United States alleged that from January 2, 2015, through January 24, 2022, the pharmacy caused the submission of claims to the Medicare Part D Program and the New Jersey Medicaid Program for drugs that were never dispensed to beneficiaries.

title: North Ridgeville Doctor Pleads Guilty to Healthcare Fraud Conspiracy
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Ohio, Northern
scheme: A doctor signed pre-completed orders for durable medical equipment and cancer genetic testing for patients he never examined, and claims totaling more than $14.5 million were billed to Medicare.

title: Florida Pharmacy Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud and Agrees to Pay More than $1 Million Settlement
scheme: OHM Pharmacy Services completed and signed Evzio prior authorization forms in place of prescribing physicians and submitted requests containing false information, including false assertions that patients had previously tried and failed Narcan or naloxone, to insurers including Medicare Part D plans.

title: Minnesota Couple Indicted in $15 Million Medical Billing Fraud Scheme
scheme: The indictment alleges the defendants overbilled Medicare, Medicaid, and other insurers for neurofeedback therapy provided through Golden Victory Medical, LLC using inapplicable medical codes, code combinations that could not be combined, and codes indicating longer service durations than provided, and laundered the proceeds.

title: Fresno County Podiatrist and Sales Representative Indicted for Conspiracy to Submit Millions of Dollars in False Claims Related to Skin Grafts
scheme: Ruiz, a podiatrist, purchased skin grafts from Aguirre and allowed Aguirre, who was not a licensed health care provider, to apply them to Medicare and Medi-Cal beneficiaries, then submitted claims falsely representing that Ruiz had applied the grafts.

title: Greensboro Woman Pleads Guilty to Health Care Fraud and Money Laundering in Connection with Multi-Million Dollar Urine Drug Testing Scheme
scheme: Hoyle billed the North Carolina Medicaid program through two businesses she owned for urine drug tests and office visits that were not performed, and used the proceeds for personal expenses.

title: Attorney General Jeff Jackson Announces Health Care Fraud And Money Laundering Guilty Plea
scheme: Jasmine Hoyle pleaded guilty to one count of health care fraud and one count of money laundering for defrauding the NC Medicaid program of more than $6 million.

title: Home health care companies owner sentenced to more than 3 years in prison for $5.7 million Medicaid fraud
scheme: While billing Medicaid for health aide services to individuals in their homes, the defendant inflated the hours of services provided, billed for registered nurses when licensed practical nurses completed the care, and billed for care for patients who were either deceased or ineligible to receive Medicaid.

title: Attorney General’s Medicaid Fraud And Vulnerable Victims Unit Secures A $1,289,679 Settlement And Corporate Oversight Of Elkton Nursing And Rehabilitation Center In Cecil County
scheme: Elkton SNF, LLC and Elkton Health Holdco, LLC d/b/a Elkton Nursing and Rehabilitation Center allegedly violated the Maryland False Health Claims Act by providing substandard care to residents.

title: Pain Management Clinic Owners and Operators Indicted on Health Care Fraud Charges
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Rhode Island
scheme: The owners and operators of a pain management clinic allegedly submitted fraudulent claims to Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, and four private insurers for purportedly medically necessary services, including acupuncture, physical therapy, and office visits, that were not actually provided to patients, in order to collect payment for massage therapy and other services not provided.

title: Kansas Doctor Admits Accepting Kickbacks to Commit Health Care Fraud
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Missouri, Eastern
scheme: A telemedicine doctor admitted accepting about $674,000 in kickbacks from five health care companies from 2017 to 2020 to order medically unnecessary durable medical equipment, pain creams and genetic tests for thousands of patients without evaluating them.

title: United States Files False Claims Act Complaint Against Vohra Wound Physicians Management and Its Owner Alleging False Claims for Wound Care Services
district: Civil Division, USAO - Florida, Southern, USAO - Georgia, Southern
scheme: The United States alleges Vohra and Dr. Ameet Vohra caused the submission of false claims to Medicare by billing nonsurgical debridements as surgical procedures through proprietary EMR software, training physicians without wound care expertise, setting revenue-based debridement targets, and automatically applying Modifier 25 to bill for exams not separately billable.

title: ALJ Upholds OIG's Demand for Stipulated Penalties from Dr. Azizulah Kamali for Breaching Integrity Agreement
scheme: An ALJ upheld OIG's demand that Dr. Kamali pay $22,000 in stipulated penalties for failing to fully and timely submit all documentation required in the first Integrity Agreement Annual Report.

title: Diagnostic Clinic of Longview Agreed to Pay $77,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: DCL employed an individual excluded from participating in any Federal health care program, a licensed vocational nurse, who provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Piedmont Health Services Agreed to Pay $4.7 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services that Did Not Meet Medicare Requirements
scheme: OIG alleged that Piedmont submitted claims to Medicare for chronic care management that failed to comply with Medicare requirements.

title: Lamoille Residents Charged With Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Stephen Maskell provided care to a Medicaid recipient he was not authorized to care for, enabling Julie Maskell to submit false timesheets to Vermont Medicaid claiming payment as though she was providing that care while she was being paid by Medicaid to care for another individual.

title: Owner of Halo Home Healthcare sentenced to 4 years in prison for health care fraud, tax crimes
scheme: Ward concealed her ownership of Halo Home Healthcare while excluded from federal health care programs and billed more than $8.5 million to Medicare, Medicaid and Veterans Affairs programs for services not performed, and provided inaccurate information causing false business tax returns.

title: Advancare Healthcare Services Agreed to Pay $41,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Advancare employed an individual excluded from participating in any Federal health care program, and that excluded registered nurse provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Lancaster County Trio Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Commit Health Care Fraud
scheme: The defendants recruited Medicaid beneficiaries as clients of Transformation Services and submitted bills and records to the State of South Carolina for behavioral health services that were never rendered, including services by unlicensed counselors.

title: Florida Man Pleads Guilty to Multi-Million Dollar Scheme to Defraud Medicare
scheme: Alston and his co-defendant unlawfully purchased Medicare beneficiary identification numbers and used them, through companies they owned and controlled, to submit over $8.4 million in claims to Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that beneficiaries did not want or request and that were ineligible for reimbursement.

title: Hospital, Medical Imaging Services Company, and Others to Pay $3.1 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: The United States alleged that the settling parties engaged in an illegal kickback and pass-through billing scheme in which Desert Imaging used Foundation Surgical Hospital's National Provider Identifier to submit claims for medical imaging services for patients with no connection to the hospital, billing them as hospital outpatient services for higher reimbursement, with the hospital retaining 17% of payments.

title: Louisiana Chiropractor Convicted of Health Care Fraud and Unemployment Insurance Fraud
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: A chiropractor solicited insured patients for advertised free chiropractic massages and billed Blue Cross Blue Shield of Louisiana over $2.3 million for services he did not perform, fabricated patient records for an audit, and falsely certified unemployment to receive pandemic benefits.

title: National Sales Director for New York-Based Mobile Diagnostic Company Pleads Guilty to Kickback Scheme
scheme: A national sales director conspired with managers of a mobile medical diagnostics company to offer and pay doctors kickbacks based on the number of transcranial doppler ultrasounds ordered, disguised through sham rental and administrative service agreements, resulting in approximately $70.6 million in fraudulent bills to Medicare.

title: Beckley Medical Clinic and Physician Agree to Pay $152,382.70 to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: Med-Surg and its owner submitted claims to Medicare and Medicaid using HCPCS code Q3014 for the telehealth originating site facility fee for telehealth visits where the patient was at home, which is not payable.

title: Florida Man Pleads Guilty to Multi-Million Dollar Scheme to Defraud Medicare
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Alston and his co-defendant unlawfully purchased Medicare beneficiary identification numbers and used them, through companies they owned and controlled, to submit over $8.4 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that beneficiaries did not want or request.

title: Worcester-Based Medical Transportation Company And Its Owner Indicted For MassHealth Fraud, Patient Abuse And Neglect, And Money Laundering
scheme: Instant Transportation, LLC and its owner allegedly submitted millions of dollars in false claims to MassHealth and its subcontractors for non-emergency medical transportation services that were never provided, laundered the funds, and abused and neglected MassHealth members.

title: Freedom Medical Labs Agreed to Be Excluded for 7 Years for Allegedly Submitting False Claims for Genetic Tests Tainted by Improper Remuneration
scheme: Freedom Medical Labs caused the submission of false claims to the Medicaid program by providing and receiving illegal remuneration tied to the referral of cancer genomic testing claims by Premier Medical, Inc. when such claims were not medically necessary and/or not performed.

title: Diligent Urgent Care Agreed to Pay $614,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Incident-to Services that Identified the Incorrect Rendering Provider and Were Upcoded
scheme: Diligent Urgent Care submitted non-physician practitioner incident-to claims for reimbursement which incorrectly identified the rendering physician and were upcoded to higher levels of service than warranted.

title: Diopsys Inc. Agrees to Pay up to $14.25 Million to Resolve Alleged Federal False Claims Act and State Law Violations Relating to Vision Testing
scheme: Diopsys caused health care providers to submit false claims to Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary electroretinography vision testing using its NOVA device, which lacked FDA clearance for that use, and made changes to the device without submitting them to FDA.

title: Attorney General James Recovers Over $5 Million From Nonprofit For Failing To Serve New York City Residents With Developmental Disabilities
scheme: Community Options billed New York's Medicaid program for day habilitation services that it failed to provide and document in compliance with state and OPWDD requirements between January 1, 2017 and September 13, 2023, and failed to return overpayments while a senior employee instructed a subordinate to create and back-date missing monthly summary notes.

title: Walgreen Co. Agrees to Pay Over $2.8 Million to Settle Allegations of Overbilling Medicaid Programs
scheme: Walgreens' pharmacies submitted inflated usual and customary prices for certain generic medications to the Massachusetts and Georgia Medicaid programs between 2008 and 2023, causing those programs to pay more than they should have.

title: Diopsys, Inc. Agrees To Pay Up To $14.25 Million To Resolve Alleged Federal False Claims Act And State Law Violations Relating To Vision Testing
scheme: Diopsys caused health care providers to submit false claims to Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary electroretinography vision testing using its NOVA device, which lacked FDA clearance for that use, and made changes to the device that were never submitted to FDA.

title: Leader Of $23 Million Health Care Fraud Scheme Pleads Guilty
scheme: Liu operated medical offices that billed Medicare and other insurance providers for acupuncture and physical therapy services that were not rendered in the manner represented or not rendered at all, using partners' insurance enrollments and paying cash kickbacks to patients and to insurer employees.

title: Acting U.S. Attorney Announces $5 Million False Claims Act Settlement With Providers Of Programs For Adults With Developmental Disabilities
scheme: The United States filed and simultaneously settled a civil False Claims Act lawsuit against Community Options, Inc. and Community Options New York, Inc., providers of programs for adults with developmental disabilities.

title: Koreatown-Based Medicare Advantage Provider Seoul Medical Group and Related Parties to Pay More Than $62 Million to Settle False Claims Lawsuit
scheme: From 2015 to 2021, Seoul Medical Group and Dr. Min Young Cha submitted false diagnosis codes for two spinal conditions, spinal enthesopathy and sacroiliitis, for patients who did not have them, and enlisted Renaissance Imaging Medical Associates to create radiology reports appearing to support the spinal enthesopathy diagnosis, increasing Medicare Advantage payments.

title: Behavioral Healthcare Company Executive Sentenced for Healthcare Fraud
scheme: Saravia directed untrained individuals to enter CPT codes for therapy services that were not provided and to upcode psychotherapy visit codes, and submitted or directed the submission of false claims to health care benefit programs.

title: Convicted Nurse Practitioner to Forfeit over $40 million from Foreign Accounts for Health Care Fraud, Money Laundering
scheme: Reddy and co-conspirators created false patient bills using the provider numbers of six doctors as treating physicians for services never provided to his medical clinics, manufactured fake medical records, and laundered the proceeds to nearly 200 bank accounts in India.

title: Medicare Advantage Provider Seoul Medical Group and Related Parties to Pay Over $62M to Settle False Claims Act Suit
scheme: Seoul Medical Group and Dr. Min Young Cha allegedly submitted diagnoses for two spinal conditions, spinal enthesopathy and sacroiliitis, for patients who did not have those conditions, and enlisted Renaissance Imaging Medical Associates to create radiology reports appearing to support the diagnoses, increasing risk-adjusted Medicare Advantage payments.

title: Attorney General Alan Wilson Announces Darlington Woman Charged With Forgery, Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Harrison, as an early interventionist with ABC's of Learning, is alleged to have signed and presented false time sheets and clinician notes indicating she provided services to multiple Medicaid beneficiaries when she had not, resulting in false claims to the South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Medical Device Manufacturer And Its Owner Agree To Pay $550,000 To Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: The defendants allegedly violated the False Claims Act by causing health care providers to bill Medicare for services in which the providers improperly re-used single-user rectal sensors and single-use catheters on multiple patients.

title: Radiology Regional Center Agreed to Pay $92,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: RRC submitted claims to Federal health care programs for services provided by an unlicensed nuclear medicine technologist.

title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Announces Arrest Of Home Services Provider For Defrauding Florida Taxpayers
scheme: The owner of a Medicaid-funded home and community services provider submitted claims to Medicaid and was paid for services never rendered to three Medicaid recipients.

title: Health Plus Was Excluded for 10 Years for Failing to Supply Payment Information Required in an OIG Subpoena
scheme: Health Plus failed to provide information required in an OIG subpoena that was necessary to determine whether Medicare payments were due and the amounts associated with those payments.

title: Cuban National Sentenced To Over Five Years In $7.6 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme
scheme: Espinosa Leon was sentenced for health care fraud and aggravated identity theft in a $7.6 million Medicare fraud scheme.

title: River Hills Man Sentenced to 21 Months’ Imprisonment for Paying Healthcare Kickbacks
scheme: Hanson and his co-defendant, owners of clinical laboratory Noah Associates, paid over $400,000 in kickbacks to the owner of a substance use treatment clinic in exchange for referrals of Medicaid and Medicare patients for urine drug testing that was not ordered by a physician or medically necessary, resulting in over $2.2 million in payments.

title: Hollywood Hills Man Sentenced to Nearly 3½ Years in Federal Prison for Paying Nearly $2.9 Million in Kickbacks for Drug Addiction Patient Referrals
scheme: Mahoney paid nearly $2.9 million in illegal kickbacks to body brokers who referred patients to his two addiction treatment facilities, concealing the payments through sham contracts while negotiating amounts based on patients' insurance reimbursements and billable treatment days.

title: Three Convicted for Fraudulently Billing Over $8 Million to Medicare and Medicaid Through Opioid Addiction Treatment Clinics in Kentucky
scheme: Through Kentucky Addiction Centers, the defendants billed Medicare and Kentucky Medicaid for medical services that were not performed or were falsely represented as more complex than the services provided, and billed for services in the name of Alzadon's father to bypass credentialing issues and use his DEA prescribing credentials to prescribe Suboxone.

title: Attorney General Bonta: Owner Of Placer County Residential Care Home Arrested And Charged With Medi-Cal Fraud
scheme: The owner and facility manager of Granite Bay Residential Care Home billed Medi-Cal for services they did not provide, received more than $500,000 in overpayments, and misappropriated program funds for personal purchases.

title: Two California Doctors Agree to Settlements Totaling $375,000 to Resolve Allegations of Fraud Schemes Related to “Electroacupuncture” Devices
scheme: Two physicians settled allegations that one solicited and received kickbacks for referring patients for Stivax electroacupuncture devices and the other's companies submitted false claims to Medicare for surgically implanted neurostimulators that were not implanted, as part of a scheme orchestrated by chiropractor Kevin Brown.

title: Assure Holdings and Assure Neuromonitoring Were Excluded for Defaulting on Payment Obligations

title: AG Nessel Secures $59.7 Million Settlement Over Kickback Allegations Against Pfizer Subsidiary
scheme: Biohaven paid kickbacks, including cash, meals, and honoraria payments, to health care providers to present at speaker programs and induce them to prescribe Nurtec ODT, causing false claims to be submitted to Medicaid and other federal health care programs.

title: Man Pleads Guilty in Connection with $17M Medicare Hospice Fraud and Home Health Care Fraud Schemes
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
scheme: Fichidzhyan and co-schemers operated sham hospice companies using stolen identities of foreign nationals as purported owners and misappropriated doctors' identifying information to submit false Medicare claims for hospice services that were not medically necessary and not provided, and he also obtained more than $1 million for his home health care agency using a doctor's name to certify beneficiaries.

title: New York Man Arrested in Dallas Airport on Healthcare Fraud Charges
district: Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, USAO - Louisiana, Eastern
scheme: Lake purchased doctors' orders for medically unnecessary orthotic braces and submitted claims to Medicare through his DME companies, and later sold doctors' orders through his marketing company in exchange for kickbacks, resulting in more than $17 million in fraudulent DME claims.

title: Hartford Substance Abuse Counselor Sentenced to 27 Months in Prison for Health Care Fraud Schemes
scheme: After being suspended from Medicaid, Epps arranged for two other licensed counselors to bill Medicaid under their provider numbers for psychotherapy services purportedly provided by her, including services never provided, in exchange for a share of the payments.

title: Attorney General Bonta Announces Nearly $60 Million Settlement Against Pfizer-Owned Pharmaceutical Holding Company, Biohaven
scheme: Biohaven provided cash payments, lavish meals, and honoraria to healthcare providers in return for prescribing Nurtec, resulting in false claims to Medicaid and other government healthcare programs from 2020 to 2022.

title: Tampa Man Agrees To Pay U.S. Government $2 Million For His Role In Medical Kickback Scheme
scheme: Taneja conspired with the owner of Oldsmar Pharmacy to enter a kickback arrangement paying a marketing company a percentage of profits from TRICARE claims it referred, causing thousands of false claims for compounded pain and scar creams to be submitted to TRICARE.

title: Arizona Couple Pleads Guilty to $1.2B Health Care Fraud
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Arizona
scheme: An Arizona couple caused over $1.2 billion in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, TRICARE, CHAMPVA and commercial insurers for medically unnecessary amniotic wound grafts applied to elderly and terminally ill patients, with over $279 million in kickbacks received from a graft distributor and kickbacks paid to sales representatives.

title: LiveCare Inc. Agrees To Pay Up To $4.9 Million To Resolve False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: LiveCare Inc. agreed to pay up to $4.9 million to resolve allegations that it violated the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act by unlawfully paying a marketing service for referrals of Medicare beneficiaries for remote patient monitoring services.

title: Attorney General Labrador Announces Settlement in Medicaid Fraud Case
scheme: Precision Diagnostics allegedly provided free drug-testing supplies to doctors in exchange for laboratory testing referrals, resulting in claims for medically unnecessary drug analysis tests submitted to the Idaho Medicaid Program between January 2013 and December 2022.

title: Woman Sentenced for Fraud Scheme Involving Claims for Unnecessary Respiratory Tests Submitted with COVID-19 Tests

scheme: Navarro and Shams caused their clinical laboratory to perform and bill approximately $369 million in respiratory pathogen panel tests that were medically unnecessary and never ordered, added to COVID-19 screening specimens, receiving about $46.7 million in reimbursement.

title: Greensboro Laboratory and Owner Agree to Pay $850,000 to Resolve Allegations of False Claims for Urine Drug Testing
scheme: The laboratory and its owner billed North Carolina Medicaid for the highest level of medically unnecessary urine drug screening tests between January 2018 and January 2022.

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Recovers More Than $55 Million in Civil Settlements and Judgments in Calendar Year 2024
scheme: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas recovered $55,969,678.60 in over 25 civil enforcement cases in 2024, including False Claims Act settlements over inflated Average Wholesale Prices for compound prescription ingredients, hospice claims for patients who were not terminally ill, inflated acupuncture bills to the Department of Veterans Affairs, kickbacks and medically unnecessary tests, and Controlled Substances Act penalties for unlawful prescriptions and recordkeeping violations.

title: Greenfield Man Sentenced to 15 Months’ Imprisonment for Paying Healthcare Kickbacks
scheme: Ali and his co-defendant, owners of clinical laboratory Noah Associates, paid over $400,000 in kickbacks to the owner of a substance use treatment clinic for referrals of Medicaid and Medicare patients for urine drug tests that were not ordered by a physician and not medically necessary, resulting in over $2.2 million in payments.

title: Philadelphia Mental Health Clinic and Its Psychiatrist Owner Agree to Pay $900,000 to Resolve False Claims Act Lawsuit for Alleged Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Defendants allegedly billed Medicaid for medication management appointments that were shorter than the required 15 minutes and falsely recorded start and end times in patient files, including overlapping times for multiple patients.

title: Florida Attorney General’s Office’s Medicaid Fraud Control Unit Secures More Than $2.2 Million for Florida Medicaid from Inpatient Behavioral Health Company
scheme: Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc. allegedly submitted false or fraudulent claims for inpatient behavioral health care to Medicaid and Medicare by admitting patients who were not eligible for inpatient treatment, failing to discharge patients who no longer needed inpatient care, and providing inadequate staffing and training.

title: Wellstar Health System Agreed to Pay $468,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Wellstar Health System submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed nurse.

title: Madison Man Sentenced to 37 Months in Prison for Conspiracy to Defraud the United States
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Mississippi, Southern
scheme: Fullwood paid kickbacks to a marketer in exchange for completed doctors' orders so his durable medical equipment company and a successor entity opened in a nominee owner's name could bill Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans for orthotic braces that were medically unnecessary and/or ineligible for reimbursement.

title: Pfizer agrees to pay nearly $60 million to resolve false claims allegations relating to improper physician payments by subsidiary
scheme: Biohaven paid remuneration, including speaker honoraria and meals at high end restaurants, to health care professionals to induce them to prescribe Nurtec ODT, causing the submission of false claims to Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: Corporation and Former Chief Executive Officer Plead Guilty to Health Care Fraud and Tax Conspiracy
district: Civil Division, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Wisconsin, Western
scheme: KBWB-Atrium and its former CEO diverted CMS funds intended for the operation, management, maintenance, and care of residents of 23 Wisconsin skilled nursing facilities for other purposes and personal expenses, and directed that taxes withheld from employees' paychecks not be paid to the IRS.

title: Pfizer Agrees to Pay Nearly 60M to Resolve False Claims Allegations Relating to Improper Physician Payments by Subsidiary
district: Civil Division, USAO - New York, Western
scheme: Biohaven paid remuneration, including speaker honoraria and meals at high end restaurants, to health care professionals to induce them to prescribe Nurtec ODT, causing the submission of false claims to Medicare and other federal health care programs.

title: C.R. Bard, Inc. and Affiliates Pay $17 Million to Resolve Allegations of Healthcare Kickbacks
scheme: The Liberator Defendants allegedly provided discounts, excessive free samples, and cost savings for in-office supplies to urology practice groups to persuade them to use Bard's "Link" prescription form for prescribing intermittent catheters, later steering those prescriptions to Bard's own DME subsidiary.

title: Operator of Home Health Care Company Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Multimillion Dollar Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Newton operated Arbor Homecare Services LLC and billed MassHealth for home health services never provided, paid kickbacks for patient referrals, entered sham employment relationships with patients' family members, and billed for services by home health aides who were not trained or certified.

title: Anesthesiology service provider pays almost $1M to settle False Claims Act liability
scheme: NWAP paid bonuses to its independently contracted pain management practices calculated from lab referral revenue, alleged as kickbacks for referrals, and submitted claims to Medicare for services resulting from those referrals in violation of the False Claims Act and Stark Law.

title: Pain-Management Doctor and Medical Practice to Pay $3.5 Million to Resolve False Claims Act and Control Substances Act Allegations
scheme: The government alleges Dr. Kabakibou and his practice billed federal health care programs for medically unnecessary and duplicative urine drug testing and pre-signed opioid prescriptions left for nurse practitioners to dispense while he was out of the country.

title: Amtrak Employee Admits Participating In $11 Million Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: An Amtrak employee received cash kickbacks from health care providers in exchange for allowing his employer health plan to be billed for services that were never provided and were not medically necessary, and recruited other employees into the scheme.

title: Walnut Creek Nursing Center Agreed to Pay $243,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Walnut Creek employed an individual who was excluded from participating in any Federal health care program, and that individual, a licensed practical nurse, provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Former nurse practitioner in Butte sentenced to five years in prison, ordered to pay more than $600,000 restitution for health care fraud
district: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Montana
scheme: A former nurse practitioner falsely billed Blue Cross Blue Shield of Montana $62,310,000 for 158 vitamin B-12 injections that did not occur, receiving $613,108, and used another nurse practitioner's DEA registration number to write prescriptions after her own license was suspended.

title: BioReference Health and OPKO Health Agree to Pay $704,349 to Settle Allegations that they Billed the Government for Medically Unnecessary Blood Tests
scheme: BioReference submitted claims for laboratory tests that had not been ordered by a patient's provider.

title: Health Care Plan Agrees to Pay Over $500,000 As Part of Self-Disclosure of Potential False Claims Act Violations
scheme: Reliance HMO provided cash payments to healthcare professionals and administrative staff at physician practices for patient contact information and paid four physicians and physician practices $2,500 each characterized as advances on coordination of care services, allegedly to induce enrollment of Medicare beneficiaries in Reliance's Medicare Advantage plan.

title: Two Charged with Defrauding Connecticut’s Medicaid Program
scheme: Apellaniz and Aponte submitted or caused to be submitted fraudulent claims to Connecticut Medicaid for applied behavior analysis services to children with Autism Spectrum Disorder that were not rendered as billed, through Minds Cornerstone LLC.

scheme: The Justice Department alleges Walgreens dispensed millions of unlawful prescriptions in violation of the Controlled Substances Act and then sought reimbursement for many of these prescriptions from federal health care programs in violation of the False Claims Act.

title: Pharmacist Guilty In $110 Million Dollar Kickback Conspiracy
scheme: A McAllen pharmacist pleaded guilty to conspiring to pay kickbacks in exchange for prescription referrals.

title: City of Livingston Agreed to Pay $116,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting False Claims for Emergency Ambulance Services

title: Action Recovery Group Agreed to Pay $73,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Action Recovery Group employed an individual excluded from Federal health care programs who, as an operations assistant, provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

scheme: Acadia submitted false claims to government healthcare programs by admitting patients not eligible for inpatient behavioral health treatment, failing to discharge patients who no longer needed inpatient care, failing to provide adequate staffing, training and supervision, and failing to provide inpatient care per federal and state regulations.

title: Two Iowa Healthcare Practitioners Settle Allegations for False Submission of Claims to Federal Healthcare Programs in Telemedicine Scheme
district: USAO - Iowa, Northern, USAO - Iowa, Southern
scheme: Two practitioners billed Medicare for office visits and medical discussions they did not provide and signed orders for medically unnecessary durable medical equipment such as orthotic braces based on recorded cold calls to beneficiaries they never contacted.

title: CHARGES: Owner of Erie County Shared-Care Homes Neglected Residents, Falsified Paperwork, and Defrauded Medicaid
scheme: Bell, licensed as a non-medical home care agency, operated shared-care homes where Medicaid consumers resided and billed for medical care by misrepresenting the qualifications of those providing care and/or where the care was rendered.

title: Doctor Sentenced for $70M Medicare Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: A doctor signed thousands of medical records and prescriptions for orthotic braces and cancer genetic tests falsely representing they were medically necessary for over 13,000 Medicare beneficiaries he did not see, speak to, or treat, which brace supply companies and laboratories used to bill Medicare more than $70 million.

title: Texas hospital CEO sentenced to federal prison for role in health care kickback conspiracy
scheme: Physicians were paid kickbacks disguised as investment returns through management services organizations in exchange for laboratory referrals to two rural Texas hospitals and an affiliated lab, which billed the tests to insurers as hospital outpatient services at higher rates.

title: Pacific Eye Institute Agreed to Pay $599,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Not Provided as Claimed or Not Medically Necessary
scheme: OIG alleged that a physician employee of Pacific Eye Institute billed for gonioscopies that were not performed or performed without the necessary gonio lens, and billed for amniotic membrane treatments for dry eye using techniques outside the standard of care without documentation sufficient to support medical necessity.

title: Doctor Sentenced for $70M Medicare Fraud Scheme
scheme: A Texas doctor prescribed durable medical equipment and cancer genetic testing without seeing, speaking to, or otherwise treating patients, in a scheme to defraud Medicare.

title: AG Nessel Reaches $19.85 Million Multistate Medicaid Fraud Settlement with Behavioral Health Facility
scheme: Acadia Healthcare Company's inpatient behavioral health facilities allegedly submitted false claims to Medicare and Medicaid by admitting patients not eligible for inpatient treatment, failing to discharge patients who no longer needed inpatient care, billing excessive lengths of stay, providing inadequate staffing and training, and failing to provide inpatient care as required by federal and state regulations.

title: Pharmacy Agrees To Resolve False Claims Act Allegations For Billing For Drugs Not Dispensed
scheme: From January 1, 2019, through January 24, 2022, Medsinbox caused the submission of claims to Medicare Part D and New Jersey Medicaid for drugs that were never dispensed to beneficiaries.

title: New Jersey Pharmacy Agrees to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations for Billing for Drugs Not Dispensed
scheme: The pharmacy agreed to resolve allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by knowingly billing federal health care programs for medications that it never dispensed.

title: Slidell Chiropractor Convicted of Health Care Fraud

scheme: Peyroux conspired with others to purchase Medicare beneficiary information and fabricated recordings of individuals posing as beneficiaries requesting over the counter COVID-19 test kits, then billed Medicare through his chiropractic clinic using the misappropriated credentials of a former nurse practitioner listed as referring provider.

scheme: Ejindu, through a durable medical equipment business operated under different names, caused the submission of false claims to North Carolina Medicaid for high-reimbursing specialized nutritional formula when recipients actually received lower-reimbursing Ensure, PediaSure, Boost, and Glucerna drinks.

title: Attorney General Jeff Jackson Files $5.5 Million Medicaid Fraud Lawsuit
scheme: Ejindu allegedly submitted claims for reimbursement to the North Carolina Medicaid program for medical supplies that were more expensive than what he actually provided to patients.

title: Attorney General’s Office Announces Sentencing of Las Vegas Couple and Behavioral Health Company for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Terrell and Marlene Drake and their company, Everton's Place dba Impossible Behavioral Health Services, were sentenced for Medicaid fraud.

title: Edinburg Doctor And Son Guilty In Kickback Conspiracy
scheme: An Edinburg physician and his son pleaded guilty to conspiring to receive kickbacks in exchange for referring prescriptions to local pharmacies.

title: Attorney General James Puts Medical Transportation Industry On Notice, Announces New Actions To Stop Ongoing Fraud
scheme: New York's Attorney General issued cease and desist notices to 54 medical transportation companies and announced four settlements totaling over $847,000 over billing Medicaid for fake trips, adding fake tolls, inflating mileage, using unlicensed drivers, and paying kickbacks to Medicaid recipients.

title: California Man Admits Role In $10 Million Health Care Kickback Scheme
scheme: Owens owned marketing companies that identified Medicare beneficiaries for at-home cancer genetic testing and received kickback payments of $1,700 to $2,000 per test reimbursed by Medicare, routed through a New Zealand company under a sham contract.

title: Chesapeake hospital indicted for healthcare fraud involving unnecessary surgical procedures
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: A federal grand jury indicted Chesapeake Regional Medical Center for healthcare fraud and conspiracy, alleging it granted and renewed privileges to Javaid Perwaiz despite knowing of his prior privilege termination for unnecessary surgeries and felony convictions, and billed health care benefit programs for medically unnecessary surgeries, pre-39-week elective inductions, misclassified inpatient surgeries, and sterilizations without valid consent forms.

title: Felisha Cunningham Sentenced For Medicaid Fraud, Theft
scheme: Cunningham was convicted and sentenced on a class A felony charge of Theft by Deception and a class B felony charge of Medicaid Fraud for false claims.

title: Connecticut Dentist Pays More than $600K to Settle False Claims Allegations
scheme: Bethi and her dental practices paid a patient recruiter $110 for each Connecticut Medicaid patient referred who received services beyond routine preventative care and submitted claims to the Connecticut Medical Assistance Program for those services.

title: Marketers And Healthcare Providers In Texas, Virginia, And South Carolina Agree To Pay Over $1.1 Million To Settle Laboratory Kickback Allegations
scheme: Two laboratory marketers and their companies allegedly paid kickbacks disguised as investment distributions from purported management service organizations to healthcare providers who ordered laboratory testing, and the providers received those payments in return for laboratory referrals, resulting in false claims to Medicare.

title: Wabash General Hospital Agreed to Pay $107,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Wabash General Hospital submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed Emergency Medical Technician.

title: Marketers and Healthcare Providers in Texas, Virginia and South Carolina Agree to Pay Over $1.1M to Settle Laboratory Kickback Allegations
scheme: Two laboratory marketers, three physicians, and a medical practice owner and associated entities agreed to pay a total of $1,137,914 to resolve False Claims Act allegations that they took part in laboratory kickback schemes in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute.

title: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to Imprisonment for Health Care Fraud
scheme: Yost dispensed cheaper generic medications while billing government health care programs for more expensive brand name drugs, billed for medications not dispensed, and rebilled returned medications without reversing the original charges.

title: Marketers and Healthcare Providers in Texas, Virginia and South Carolina Agree to Pay Over $1.1M to Settle Laboratory Kickback Allegations
scheme: Laboratory marketers and their companies paid kickbacks, disguised as investment distributions from purported management service organizations, to physicians and a clinic owner in return for laboratory testing referrals, resulting in false claims to Medicare.

title: Owner of Addiction Treatment Chain That Billed for Recovery Services Not Provided Sentenced to More Than Eight Years in Federal Prison in Health Care Fraud Conspiracy
scheme: Brier and his addiction treatment company billed Medicare, Medicaid, and other insurers for 45-minute counseling sessions that were not provided or lasted only a few minutes, and submitted a Medicare application concealing Brier's role and prior conviction.

title: Adriana Strimbu, DPM Agreed to Pay $41,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Dr. Strimbu employed an individual excluded from participating in any Federal health care program, a receptionist who provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Physicians Toxicology Laboratory And Its Owners To Pay $4.425 Million To Settle Allegations Of Unnecessary Drug Testing
scheme: PTL caused physicians to order medically unnecessary urine drug testing and hormone testing and submitted claims for reimbursement to the Medicare Program for those tests.

title: Telehealth Company Pays $386,000 to Resolve Allegations of Overbilling for Medicare Telehealth Time
scheme: The United States alleged that between January 1, 2017, and November 30, 2022, Meditelecare submitted and caused the submission of claims to Medicare for telehealth psychotherapy sessions that did not meet the minimum time requirements for payment and relied on false time records in support of those services.

title: Operations Manager Pleads Guilty to Kickback Scheme
scheme: Doyle conspired with managers of a mobile medical diagnostics company to offer and pay doctors kickbacks, disguised as rental and administrative service agreements, based on the number of transcranial doppler brain scans they ordered.

title: Virginia Beach doctor agrees to $625,000 False Claims Act settlement
scheme: Saffold and Chesapeake Bay ENT billed federal and state payors for balloon sinus dilations that were not medically necessary, staged procedures to increase reimbursement, and billed endoscopies with sphenoid sinusoscopy under CPT Code 31235 when that service was not performed.

title: Attorney General Tong Announces New Haven Psychiatrist to Pay More Than 450K to Settle False Claims and Controlled Substances Act
scheme: Syed issued medically unnecessary prescriptions, including controlled substances, causing false claims to be submitted by Cornerstone Pharmacy (d/b/a Whalley Drug) to Medicare and Medicaid, and billed Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary office visits related to those prescriptions.

scheme: The owners of R&B Medical Group, Universal Diagnostic Laboratories, and Southern California Medical Center are alleged to have submitted false claims to Medicare and Medi-Cal from 2014 to 2021 by paying third-party marketers to induce patient referrals, paying kickbacks for referrals, and self-referring patients to their own laboratories.

title: New Haven Psychiatrist to Pay More Than $450K to Settle False Claims Act and Controlled Substances Act Allegations
scheme: Syed issued medically unnecessary prescriptions, including for controlled substances, causing false claims to be submitted by a pharmacy to Medicare and Medicaid, and billed Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary office visits, and issued controlled substance prescriptions without a legitimate medical purpose.

title: Falanda Shelton Agreed to Be Excluded for 7 Years for Allegedly Paying Improper Remuneration
scheme: Shelton paid remuneration to marketers for patient leads and then knowingly presented to Medicare claims for durable medical equipment that she knew or should have known were medically unnecessary.

title: Central Home Health Care Agreed to Pay $29,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: CHHC submitted claims to Medicare for services provided by an unlicensed nurse.

scheme: OIG alleged that Golder Ranch Fire District submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed paramedic.

scheme: An employee of NormaTec improperly created prescribing physicians' orders for durable medical equipment and medical records and other documentation supporting medical necessity that should have been created by the prescribing physician, and NormaTec submitted and received payment for certain claims for that DME from Federal health care programs.

scheme: Cardiovascular Specialists and Dr. Katz allegedly engaged in improper "incident-to" billing by submitting claims to Medicare for E&M services under Dr. Katz' NPI that were performed by nurse practitioners when he was not in the clinic supervising them, and submitted claims to Medicare and TRICARE for E&M services that should have been billed at a lower reimbursement level.

title: Sharp Healthcare Agreed to Pay $153,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: Sharp Healthcare employed an individual, a nurse, who was excluded from participating in any Federal health care program and who provided items or services that were billed to Federal health care programs.

title: Southern California-Based Clinics, Laboratory and Their Owners to Pay $10M for False Claims Arising from Kickbacks and Self-Referrals
scheme: The defendants submitted false claims to Medicare and Medi-Cal arising from paying kickbacks and making self-referrals.

scheme: Santiam Memorial Hospital submitted claims to Medicare for ambulance services without a beneficiary, or their authorized representative, authorizing Santiam to submit claims to Medicare and accept assignment on behalf of the patient.

title: Drug Wholesaler Agrees to $1.5 Million Settlement of Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act Allegations
scheme: The United States alleges that from 2013 to 2018 the defendant induced the sale of its pain creams to physicians by offering them at or near cost, billing the Department of Labor's Office of Workers' Compensation Programs on behalf of the physicians at an exorbitant markup and then splitting the reimbursement with the physicians.

title: Food City Agrees To Pay Over $8 Million To Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related To Opioid Dispensing
scheme: From Jan. 1, 2011, through Dec. 31, 2018, 24 Food City store pharmacies dispensed opioids and other controlled substances that were medically unnecessary, lacked a legitimate medical purpose or medically accepted indication, and/or were not dispensed pursuant to valid prescriptions, resulting in false claims to federal healthcare programs.

title: Inform Diagnostics Agrees to Pay $2.9 Million to Resolve Potential False Claims Act Liability for Self-Reported Violations
scheme: Inform Diagnostics self-disclosed conduct that potentially violated the Anti-Kickback Statute, resulting in the submission of false claims for payment to Medicare and other federal health care programs.

district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Puerto Rico
scheme: MMM Holdings distributed gift cards to administrative assistants of providers to induce the referral, recommendation, or arrangement for enrollment of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries in an MMM Medicare Advantage plan and submitted or caused claims for payment to Medicare.

title: Food City Agrees to Pay over $8M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Opioid Dispensing
scheme: From Jan. 1, 2011, through Dec. 31, 2018, 24 Food City store pharmacies dispensed opioids and other controlled substances that were medically unnecessary, lacked a legitimate medical purpose or medically accepted indication, and/or were not dispensed pursuant to valid prescriptions, resulting in false claims to federal health care programs.

title: Sartell Woman Pleads Guilty in Bank Fraud Case
scheme: Starin submitted fraudulent claims for reimbursement to TRICARE through her business Baby's on Broadway and, when TRICARE began rejecting claims, created fake invoices from a shell company called Sunshine Medical LLC to obtain over $9,000,000 in financing from two lenders.

title: Jamestown Pharmacist Arrested and Charged with Health Care Fraud and Aggravated Identity Theft in a Multi-Million Dollar Health Care Fraud Scheme
scheme: Hall submitted false claims to Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, and Blue Cross Blue Shield for prescriptions for drugs that were medically unnecessary, not actually dispensed, or not ordered by a physician or other healthcare provider, and used other people's identification without authorization to obtain reimbursement.

title: Food City Agrees to Pay over $8M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Opioid Dispensing
scheme: Food City agreed to settle False Claims Act allegations related to its dispensing of opioids and other controlled substances and claims paid by federal and state health care programs.

scheme: MacEachron edited claim forms to add units of service beyond those actually performed and submitted them to insurance companies and TRICARE for payment for physical therapy services that were not provided.

scheme: Sixteen cardiology practices and associated physicians agreed to pay a total of $17,761,564 to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by overbilling Medicare for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals.

scheme: Evergreen Recovery's leaders are accused of overbilling DHS and UCare for substance abuse treatment services that Evergreen did not deliver and steering clients to a sober housing provider controlled by one of Evergreen's owners in exchange for attending billable programming.

district: Civil Division, USAO - District of Columbia, USAO - Kentucky, Western

title: Rapid Health Agrees to Pay $8.2M for Allegedly Billing Medicare for Over-the-Counter COVID-19 Tests That Were Not Provided to Beneficiaries
scheme: Rapid Health knowingly submitted or caused the submission of false claims to Medicare for over-the-counter Covid-19 tests that were never provided to Medicare beneficiaries under the CMS OTC Covid-19 Test Demonstration Project.

title: Sixteen Cardiology Practices to Pay a Total of $17.7M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations Concerning Inflated Medicare Reimbursements
scheme: Sixteen cardiology practices and associated physicians agreed to pay a total of $17,761,564 to resolve allegations that they reported inflated acquisition costs to Medicare Part B for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals.

scheme: Rapid Health knowingly submitted or caused the submission of false claims to Medicare for over-the-counter COVID-19 tests that were not provided to Medicare beneficiaries.
