title: Former Doctor and Her Wife Sentenced for Fraud and Other Crimes
scheme: A doctor and her wife, who owned the medical practice, billed insurers for office visits under the doctor's name when she did not see the patients, and later obtained COVID-19 disaster relief funds for a closed practice, while the doctor also unlawfully distributed opioids.

title: Three Indicted In Medicaid Fraud Conspiracy Scheme
scheme: Three defendants used an outpatient drug and alcohol treatment center, Evergreen Recovery, Inc., to overbill Medicaid and other health care programs for treatment that was not provided or not eligible for reimbursement, using free housing in controlled sober homes as a kickback to induce clients to enroll and attend sessions, and creating backdated electronic health record entries.

title: AG Campbell Announces $2 Million Settlement With SaVida Health To Resolve Allegations Of False Billing To MassHealth
scheme: SaVida Health submitted false claims to MassHealth and MassHealth managed care entities by billing for more expensive office visits than provided and billing for medically unnecessary urine drug tests.

title: Norton Clark Hospital Agreed to Pay $768,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Remuneration to Physicians in the Form of Office Expenses
scheme: OIG alleged that Norton Clark Hospital paid remuneration to physicians and physician practices in the form of certain maintenance and other business expenses in a jointly owned office building.

title: Nine Charged In $20 Million Medicaid/Medicare Fraud Scheme Perpetrated At South Philadelphia Pharmacy
scheme: Nine individuals were charged in connection with a $20 million Medicaid and Medicare fraud scheme stemming from a South Philadelphia neighborhood pharmacy.

title: Justice Department Files Nationwide Lawsuit Alleging CVS Knowingly Dispensed Controlled Substances in Violation of the Controlled Substances Act and the False Claims Act
district: Civil Division, USAO - Rhode Island, USAO - Virginia, Eastern
scheme: The complaint alleges that from Oct. 17, 2013, to the present CVS knowingly filled prescriptions for controlled substances that lacked a legitimate medical purpose, were not valid, and/or were not issued in the usual course of professional practice, and sought reimbursement from federal healthcare programs for those prescriptions.

title: Justice Department Files Nationwide Lawsuit Alleging CVS Knowingly Dispensed Controlled Substances In Violation Of The Controlled Substances Act And The False Claims Act
scheme: The complaint alleges CVS filled unlawful prescriptions for controlled substances in violation of the Controlled Substances Act and sought reimbursement from federal health care programs for those unlawful prescriptions in violation of the False Claims Act.

title: The Endoscopy Center Agreed to Pay $1.3 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in the Form of Supplies, Equipment, and Insurance Reimbursement
scheme: OIG alleged that The Endoscopy Center received remuneration from an anesthesia practice in the form of anesthesia supplies, equipment, and commercial insurance reimbursement that was due to the anesthesia practice for services the anesthesia practice rendered.

title: Brookside Medical Home Visits Agreed to Pay $167,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in the Form of Rebates
scheme: Brookside received rebates from a biologic products manufacturer based on the net volume of skin graft products purchased, and used the manufacturer's invoices that did not reflect the rebates when seeking reimbursement from Federal health care programs.

title: Hakop Oganyan, MD and Holy Medical Center Agreed to Pay $627,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Bundled Services that Included Drugs that Were Not Purchased
scheme: Dr. Oganyan and HMC submitted claims to Medicare Part B and Medicaid for the provision and administration of Spravato under HCPCS Code G2082 when they did not purchase the Spravato, rather specialty pharmacies delivered the Spravato to HMC and submitted claims for the Spravato to Medicare Part D and Medicaid.

title: Tampa General Hospital Agreed to Pay $442,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed and Unqualified Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Tampa General Hospital submitted claims for biofeedback therapy services performed by an unlicensed and unqualified professional.

title: Conservatory of Hope, Amber Galbraith, and Heath Lewis Agreed to Be Excluded for 35 Years for Allegedly Submitting False Claims
scheme: OIG alleged the parties submitted claims for services rendered by unqualified providers, claims lacking supporting documentation, and claims for services not provided as claimed.

title: Piedmont Eastside Hospital Agreed to Pay $21,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Piedmont Eastside Hospital submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed nurse.

title: Pasadena Doctor Agrees to Plead Guilty to Conspiring with Attorney to Bilk More Than $3 Million from California’s Workers’ Compensation Fund
scheme: Do agreed to plead guilty to conspiring to defraud California's Subsequent Injuries Benefits Trust Fund by continuing to draft workers' compensation medical reports for Liberty Medical Group after his suspension, with other doctors' names listed on the billing forms and reports mailed for payment, and to filing a false 2021 tax return omitting approximately $66,227 of income.

title: Attorney General Ford Announces Sentencing of Las Vegas Woman for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Jackson was adjudicated guilty of Submitting False Claims: Medicaid Fraud and ordered to pay $100,000 with a suspended 12-48 month term of incarceration.

title: Santa Paula Doctor Sentenced to 2 Years in Federal Prison for Role in Hospice Fraud that Bilked Medicare Out of $3.2 Million
scheme: A physician falsely certified that patients had terminal illnesses so two hospice companies could submit approximately $3,917,946 in fraudulent claims to Medicare for medically unnecessary hospice services, of which about $3,289,889 was paid.

title: Doctor Pleads Guilty in $5.5M COVID-19 Fraud Scheme
scheme: A Texas physician pleaded guilty in connection with his role in a $5.5 million over-the-counter COVID-19 test fraud scheme.

title: Doctor Pleads Guilty in $5.5M COVID-19 Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section, USAO - Texas, Eastern
scheme: A physician purchased Medicare beneficiary identifiers and used them to bill Medicare more than $5.5 million for over-the-counter COVID-19 test kits that were medically unnecessary and often not requested by beneficiaries.

title: Additional Charges Brought Against Boston Dental Manager, Including Prescription And Credit Card Fraud
scheme: Additional indictments were brought against the manager of a Boston dental practice for unauthorized issuance of prescriptions and unauthorized use of a patient's credit card, following earlier indictments against him and the practice for Medicaid fraud, larceny, unlicensed practice of dentistry, and assault and battery.

title: United States Settles False Claims Act Allegations Against Pharmaceutical Distributor For Paying Kickbacks Through Inventory Management Systems
scheme: ASD, doing business as Besse Medical, provided inventory management systems to retina practices at no cost to induce them to purchase drugs from Besse, in alleged violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act.

title: Florence Wellness and JBH Holdings Agreed to Pay $240,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting False Claims Related to Remote Patient Monitoring Services
scheme: OIG alleged that Florence billed the Medicare program for remote patient monitoring services without having obtained at least 16 days of biometric readings within a 30-day period as required by Medicare.

title: ASD Specialty Healthcare (D/B/A Besse Medical) Agrees To Pay $1.67 Million for Allegedly Paying Kickbacks to Retina Practices
scheme: ASD Specialty Healthcare, doing business as Besse Medical, provided an inventory management system known as PODIS at no cost to retina practices that entered into prime vendor agreements to purchase a percentage of their specialty drugs from ASD, allegedly causing physicians to submit false claims to Medicare, TRICARE and the Department of Veterans Affairs.

title: Whitefish doctor sentenced for defrauding Medicare and other federal health programs
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Montana
scheme: Dean was paid by a telemedicine company to sign orders for durable medical equipment that patients did not need, and he fraudulently charged Medicare, CHAMPVA and Railroad Retirement Board programs for telemedicine office visits that did not occur while also authorizing unnecessary covid tests.

title: Sagis Agreed to Pay $1.1 Million for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Receiving Remuneration in Exchange for Using a Reference Laboratory
scheme: OIG alleged that Sagis' former owner and CEO received remuneration from a laboratory in exchange for Sagis using the laboratory as its reference laboratory for epidermal nerve fiber density testing.

title: Glendale Woman and Lakewood Man Found Guilty of $3.2 Million Hospice Fraud Scheme Involving Kickbacks for Patient Referrals
scheme: Palma, while excluded from Medicare, concealed her ownership of Magnolia Gardens Hospice and paid marketers including Abrams kickbacks for patient referrals that resulted in approximately $3.2 million in fraudulent claims to Medicare for purported hospice care for patients who were not dying.

title: California Hospital to Pay $10.25M to Resolve False Claims Allegations
scheme: Oroville Hospital allegedly submitted false claims to Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary inpatient admissions, paid physician bonuses that took into account the volume or value of admissions, and used erroneous SIRS diagnosis codes.

title: Naimetulla Ahmed Syed, MD Agreed to Be Excluded for 20 Years for Allegedly Prescribing Medically Unnecessary Drugs and Related False Claims
scheme: Syed issued medically unnecessary prescriptions, including controlled substance prescriptions, causing a pharmacy to submit false claims to Medicare and Medicaid, and billed Medicare and Medicaid for medically unnecessary office visits related to those prescriptions.

title: Owner of Milford Chiropractic Clinic Pleads Guilty to Federal Health Care Fraud Offense
district: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), USAO - Delaware
scheme: Moise paid patients who had been in recent car accidents to attend treatment sessions at his chiropractic clinic irrespective of need and concealed those payments from insurance companies while employees submitted claims for reimbursement under Delaware's no-fault PIP law.

title: New York Doctor Pleads Guilty to Receiving Kickbacks
scheme: An internist ordered hundreds of medically unnecessary transcranial doppler brain scans using false diagnoses in exchange for cash kickbacks of approximately $100 per test, resulting in approximately $1 million in fraudulent bills to Medicare and private insurance companies.

title: Oroville Hospital to Pay $10.25 Million to Resolve Allegations of Kickbacks and False Billing
scheme: Oroville Hospital allegedly paid bonuses to physicians based on the number of patients they admitted and submitted claims to Medicare and Medi-Cal for medically unnecessary inpatient admissions and claims containing false SIRS diagnosis codes.

title: California Hospital To Pay $10.25M To Resolve False Claims Allegations
scheme: Oroville Hospital agreed to pay $10,250,000 to resolve allegations that it knowingly submitted false claims to Medicare and Medicaid arising from medically unnecessary inpatient hospital admissions, a kickback and physician self-referral scheme and the use of erroneous diagnosis codes.

title: New York-Based Businessman Admits $5.3 Million Health Care Fraud And Kickback Conspiracy
scheme: Chaudhari owned a New York-based consulting company that purchased Medicare beneficiary information and sold it to medical providers who submitted Medicare claims for over-the-counter COVID-19 tests that beneficiaries did not need or order, concealed through sham agreements and fraudulent invoices.

title: Pharmacies In Granby And Dorchester To Pay Over $500,000 To Resolve Allegations Of False Billing To MassHealth
scheme: Two independent retail pharmacies submitted false claims to MassHealth, the state's Medicaid program.

title: Colorado Springs Nurse Practitioner Agrees To Pay $90K To Resolve Allegations Of Improper Prescribing Of Controlled Substances
scheme: A nurse practitioner agreed to pay $90,000 to resolve allegations that she unlawfully prescribed controlled substances, including opioids and drug combinations, in violation of the Controlled Substances Act and False Claims Act.

title: Attorney General Josh Stein Reaches $825,000 Health Care Fraud Settlement
scheme: Carter Clinic, P.A., and its owner submitted false claims to the North Carolina Medicaid program.

title: Bay Area Home Health Agency Owner Sentenced To Two Years In Prison For Health Care Fraud
scheme: Katz submitted false documentation to Medicare, used licensed practitioners' identities without consent, had non-Registered Nurses prepare Start of Care forms and manipulated records to appear RNs completed them, and billed Medicare for physical therapy services not provided.

title: Attorney General Ford Announces Sentencing of Las Vegas Woman and Behavioral Health Company for Medicaid Fraud
scheme: Rodneshia Carter and her company Love & Loyalty LLC were sentenced for Medicaid fraud.

title: Neurologist pays nearly $1M to settle false billing allegations for electro-acupuncture devices
scheme: Hamid billed Medicare for surgical implantation of neurostimulator electrodes when patients instead received electro-acupuncture devices taped behind the ear in his clinic with no incision made.

title: Telemarketer Sentenced For $67M Health Care Fraud And Money Laundering Scheme
scheme: A Florida man participated in a conspiracy to defraud Medicare by billing over $67 million for medically unnecessary genetic testing.

title: Telemarketer Sentenced for $67M Health Care Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Goyos managed the "doctor chase" division of a call center that tricked physicians into ordering medically unnecessary genetic tests, and he and co-conspirators submitted over $67 million in false claims to Medicare.

title: Telemarketer Sentenced for $67M Health Care Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme
scheme: A telemarketing call center manager directed employees to deceive physicians into ordering medically unnecessary genetic tests, and he and co-conspirators submitted over $67 million in false claims to Medicare.

title: Home Health Care Company and Its Owners Pay More Than $360K to Settle False Claims Allegations
scheme: Home Care VNA, Lubega, and Ogutt submitted or caused to be submitted claims for reimbursement to Connecticut Medicaid for home health care services for patients who had unsigned plans of care or had no plans of care at all.

title: Attorney General James Announces Convictions And Sentences Of Five Taxi Company Owners In Orange And Rensselaer Counties For Stealing Millions From Medicaid
scheme: Five taxi company owners and their seven transportation companies pleaded guilty to billing Medicaid for fictitious trips, fake tolls and fabricated mileage, paying kickbacks to Medicaid recipients for their identification numbers, and laundering the proceeds through shell companies.

title: Podiatrist and Patient Recruiter Sentenced for $8.5M Compounding Fraud Scheme
district: Criminal Division, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: A podiatrist signed prescriptions for compounded pain and scar creams for TRICARE beneficiaries he never spoke to, examined, or treated, and a patient recruiter recruited him and the beneficiaries, causing a Fort Worth-based pharmacy to bill TRICARE approximately $8.5 million.

title: United States and State of Oklahoma File False Claims Act Complaint Against OKC Laboratory and Director
scheme: The complaint alleges the laboratory and its director submitted or caused the submission of false and/or fraudulent claims for payment to Government Health Benefit Programs for testing services that were not rendered or not reimbursable.

title: Colorado Springs Man Sentenced To Eight Years’ Probation For Illegally Billing Medicaid For Patients With Developmental Disabilities
scheme: Craft fraudulently acquired $122,441 through falsified medical billing to Medicaid for patients with developmental disabilities between 2020 and 2023.

title: Freeman Health System to Freeman West Agreed to Pay $250,000 for Allegedly Violating Patient Dumping Statute by Failing to Provide Stabilizing Treatment
scheme: OIG alleged that Freeman failed to provide stabilizing treatment to a pregnant patient who presented to its labor and delivery unit with preterm premature rupture of membranes and requested induction of labor, instead offering only observation until her condition deteriorated.

title: Podiatrist and Patient Recruiter Sentenced for $8.5M Compounding Fraud Scheme
scheme: A podiatrist and a patient recruiter were sentenced for a scheme to fraudulently bill TRICARE for compounded creams that were medically unnecessary and procured through kickbacks and bribes.

title: Florida Physician Assistant Pleads Guilty to a $7.3 Million Health Care Fraud Conspiracy
scheme: Jordan, a physician assistant working for a Florida-based telemedicine company, agreed to electronically sign doctor's orders for cancer genetic testing regardless of medical necessity and without a pre-existing provider-patient relationship, and those orders were used to submit more than $7.3 million in false claims to Medicare.

title: $2 Million Resolves Kickback Allegations Relating to Denver Neuromonitoring Company
scheme: Assure paid remuneration to surgeons through joint venture companies to induce them to order intraoperative neuromonitoring services, resulting in claims submitted to federally funded healthcare programs.

title: Operations Manager Charged in Kickback Scheme
scheme: Doyle allegedly conspired with managers of a mobile medical diagnostics company to offer and pay kickbacks to doctors, disguised through sham rental and administrative service agreements, in exchange for ordering medically unnecessary transcranial doppler brain scans billed to Medicare.

title: Bedford Regional Urology Agreed to Pay $463,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Incident-to Services Without Proper Supervision
scheme: Bedford Urology submitted claims for physician assistant services that did not qualify for "incident to" payments because the physician did not directly supervise the physician assistant providing the services.

title: Multiple Conspirators Sentenced In $54.3 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme
scheme: The defendants owned and operated pharmacies that paid kickbacks and bribes to telemarketers and telemedicine providers to secure orders for medically unnecessary prescriptions, mainly topical creams, that were billed to Medicare Part D, sometimes recycled through multiple pharmacies they controlled.

title: American Health Imaging, Inc. and Scott Arant to Pay Over $5 Million to Resolve Allegations of Healthcare Kickbacks
scheme: AHI and its former founder and CEO provided physicians with meals, tickets to sporting events, and other gifts and entered into above fair market value personal services agreements with referring physicians to induce referrals of diagnostic scans to AHI's independent diagnostic testing facilities.

title: Lake Cumberland Regional Hospital Agreed to Pay $587,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by Unlicensed Individuals
scheme: After self-disclosing to OIG, the hospital agreed to pay for allegedly submitting claims for services provided by an unlicensed social worker and an unlicensed behavioral health therapist.

title: Lumberton-based Behavioral Health Provider Agrees to Pay over $2.5 Million to Settle Medicaid Fraud Allegations
scheme: Southeastern and the Hutchinsons submitted claims to North Carolina Medicaid for services that were not rendered, including for patients who were incarcerated or deceased on the billed dates of service, without supporting medical records.

title: Mary Hitchcock Memorial Hospital Agreed to Pay $20,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: After self-disclosing to OIG, the hospital agreed to pay $20,000 for allegedly employing an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: El Paso Medical Equipment Supplier Sentenced to Federal Prison for $1.7 Million Healthcare Fraud Scheme
scheme: An El Paso medical equipment supplier was sentenced to 60 months in prison for conspiracy to commit healthcare fraud involving $1.7 million.

title: Tanner Medical Centered Agreed to Pay $118,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: OIG alleged that Tanner Medical Center, Inc. submitted claims for inpatient hospital services provided by a registered nurse when they were not licensed as a registered nurse in the State of Georgia.

title: Attorney General Josh Stein Reaches $2.5 Million Medicaid Fraud Settlement
scheme: Southeastern Behavioral Healthcare Services, LLC and its owners allegedly submitted false claims to the North Carolina Medicaid program.

title: New York Doctor Charged for Receiving Kickbacks
scheme: Seodat allegedly conspired with a mobile medical diagnostics company principal to order hundreds of medically unnecessary transcranial doppler brain scans using false diagnoses in exchange for cash kickbacks of approximately $100 per test, resulting in approximately $1 million in fraudulent bills to Medicare and private insurers.

title: Solco Healthcare Agreed to Pay $200,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Failing to Submit Timely Pricing Data
scheme: Solco failed to submit timely certified monthly and quarterly Average Manufacturer's Price data to CMS for certain months and quarters in 2021, 2022, and 2023.

title: Neurosurgeon pays $2M to settle allegations involving false procedures
scheme: Bindal billed Medicare and the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program for surgical implantation of neurostimulator electrodes when patients instead received electro-acupuncture devices taped behind the ear, sometimes placed by a device sales representative or physician assistant in his clinic.

title: Classic Lifeguard Agreed to Pay $370,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Paying Remuneration in the Form of Purported Compensation
scheme: OIG alleged that Classic Lifeguard paid remuneration to two individuals in the form of purported employment compensation where services were not provided as contemplated by the arrangement.

title: Doctor Sentenced To Five Years In Prison For Defrauding The NBA Players’ Health And Welfare Benefit Plan
scheme: Washington, a licensed medical doctor operating clinics in the Seattle area, generated fraudulent invoices for nearly $500,000 of medical services he never provided to retired NBA players and swiped Plan-issued debit cards to collect over $450,000 from the NBA Players' Health and Welfare Benefit Plan.

title: Attorney General Ken Paxton’s Investigation Results in 10-Year Prison Sentence and Over $34 Million Restitution for North Texas Doctor
scheme: Canchola received kickbacks to electronically sign durable medical equipment and cancer genomic testing authorizations for patients he had never seen, which were used to submit over $54 million in false claims.

title: Fort Lauderdale Man Pleads Guilty To Conspiring To Defraud Medicare In The Provision Of COVID-19 Test Kits
scheme: Wills and a co-conspirator operated a company that connected marketers who illegally obtained Medicare beneficiary identifying information with medical service providers who shipped COVID-19 tests to those beneficiaries, billed Medicare, and paid per-beneficiary kickbacks.

title: North Alabama-Shoals Hospital Agreed to Pay $194,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Submitting Claims for Services Provided by an Unlicensed Individual
scheme: Shoals submitted claims for services provided by an unlicensed social worker.

title: Three Plymouth Women Arraigned On Charges Related To Fatal Elder Neglect Case
scheme: The three women, who were responsible for the wellbeing of 79-year-old Dinora Cardoso, failed to properly care for her, which led to her death, and were charged with manslaughter, caretaker neglect of an elder, larceny, and Medicaid fraud.

title: Michigan Woman Convicted of $1.4M Health Care Kickback Scheme
scheme: A Michigan woman was convicted for her role in a conspiracy to defraud the United States and receive illegal health care kickbacks.

title: Michigan Woman Convicted of $1.4M Health Care Kickback Scheme
district: Civil Rights - Criminal Section, Criminal - Criminal Fraud Section
scheme: Smettler-Bolton referred Medicare beneficiaries to several Metro Detroit home health companies in exchange for kickbacks paid by the owners and operators, causing over $1.4 million of loss to Medicare.

title: Federal Judge Sentences Charlotte Licensed Clinical Social Worker To 11+ Years In Prison For Medicaid Fraud, COVID-19 Fraud, And Money Laundering
scheme: Cross, through her company Odyssey Health Group, submitted fraudulent reimbursement claims to South Carolina Medicaid for rehabilitative behavioral health services that were never provided using beneficiaries' personal identifying information, created fake clinical notes, laundered proceeds, and obtained fraudulent PPP loans.

title: SummitStone Health Partners Agreed to Pay $181,000 for Allegedly Violating the Civil Monetary Penalties Law by Employing an Excluded Individual
scheme: SummitStone Health Partners self-disclosed that it employed an individual that it knew or should have known was excluded from participation in Federal health care programs.

title: Four Individuals Indicted for Conspiracy to Commit Healthcare Fraud At Sober Homes
scheme: Indictment alleges the owner and associates of a sober home company solicited kickbacks for referring urine drug tests to laboratories and caused approximately $26.7 million in medically unnecessary urine drug tests, plus peer support services not properly provided, to be billed to Medicare and Kentucky Medicaid.

title: Fresno Doctors Agree to Pay $2.4 Million to Resolve Kickback Allegations
scheme: Fresno physicians solicited and received payments described as investment returns from management service organizations controlled by Matthew H. Peters in exchange for directing prescriptions to Peters' mail-order pharmacies, and one physician also billed Medicare for non-covered peripheral venous studies under evaluation and management codes.

title: Local Home Healthcare Company Owner Accused of $800,000 Fraud
scheme: The owner of a home healthcare company submitted hundreds of fraudulent claims to Missouri Medicaid and the VA Community Care Network for services that were never provided, including claims for patients who were hospitalized and claims for more than 24 hours of care in a single day.
